title: Interactive Three.js Koi Pond
author: SouranyStudio
prompt:
Build an ultra-realistic, interactive Japanese koi pond garden as ONE self-contained HTML file named koi-pond.html. No build step, no bundler, no asset folder: every texture, mesh, sound and animation is generated procedurally in the file. The only external loads are three.js r160 UMD from cdnjs (https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/0.160.0/three.min.js) and dat.gui 0.7.9 from cdnjs. Target 60 fps on a laptop GPU at 1.6x device pixel ratio.

Work in rounds. After every implementation round: run it in a browser, take screenshots, measure (fps, frame time, and any metric the round defines), fix what the screenshots show, and only then move on. Commit to git after each round with an imperative subject and a body that explains what changed and why. Do not stop at "it renders": self-verify until the screenshots match the references below.

== 0. File layout ==
One <script> in sections, in this order: parameters & constants; math/noise utilities (hash, value noise, fbm2/fbm3, smoothstep, lerp, clamp, Catmull-Rom interpolation); procedural textures (canvas + DataTexture, height-to-normal); geometry helpers (merge, tube, lathe); renderer/sky/sun/environment; shared material injections; terrain + basin; stones; bridge + pavilion; vegetation; water (sim, shader, passes); koi; post-processing; camera, dive & audio; GUI, quality, main loop.

== 1. Renderer, sky, sun ==
WebGLRenderer, HDR half-float main target with 4x MSAA (2x on Low), ACES tone mapping, exposure 0.9. PCFSoft shadow map 4096 (2048 on Low), updated every other frame through a camera that sees every layer. Preetham analytic sky (after three.js Sky.js) plus an FBM cloud deck lit brighter toward the sun with crude self-shadowing. Sun from time of day (6-19 h, default 10.5) and azimuth (default 55 deg). Environment map re-baked from the sky when the sun moves. Directional sun intensity ~3.3 plus a hemisphere light.

Render layers, every mesh on exactly one: ABOVE=1, UNDER=2, BOTH=3, WATER=4, SKY=5, SURFACE=6 (things lying on the water: pads, petals; never mirrored).

== 2. Shared material injections (patchMaterial) ==
One onBeforeCompile helper used by every MeshPhysical/Standard material. It injects: world-position/normal varyings; optional wind sway in a replaced project_vertex (slow sway * per-vertex weight + gusts travelling along the wind + fast leaf flutter); a FLOAT mode where the vertex rides the water surface (same Gerstner sum + ripple texture as the water); underwater lighting computed before the light loop: Beer-Lambert on the refracted sun path, caustics projected along the refracted sun ray (two counter-scrolling Voronoi patterns multiplied, slight chromatic dispersion growing with depth), ambient attenuation with depth (barely dimmed in the first 5 cm), analytic soft koi shadows (see section 6); after the light loop: submerged surfaces lose ~88% of specular; exponential teal absorption fog when the camera is submerged; weather albedo/roughness (snow cover on up-facing surfaces, wet darkening + puddle sheen, autumn tint). Global uniforms shared by every patched material: uTime, uWaterY=0, uSunDir, uSunDirW (refracted), uSunColor, uAbsorb, uScatter, uInscatter, uCamUnder, tCaustics, uWindDir, uWind, uGust, uSnowCover, uWet, uAutumn, uFogDensity, uFogColor, uRain, uIce, uKoiA[20], uKoiB[20]. Options: tri (triplanar rock shading), hedge, leaf (translucency: back-lit leaves glow with the shadowed sun colour), wood (weathering), and a matching depth material for shadow casting that repeats the same vertex deformation.

== 3. Terrain, pond, stones, architecture ==
Pond outline: a closed Catmull-Rom curve sampled to 480 points, with a signed-distance field (sdf) built from it and stored as a 256x256 mask texture; a heightfield ripple sim of N=256 covering a 13.4 m square. Terrain: displaced plane, pond basin depth up to ~1.2 m, pebble floor, mossy banks, granite coping stones around the rim. Boulders: lathe/noise rocks with granite grain, cracks, pits and lichen (triplanar), some breaking the surface. A wooden arched bridge across the pond, a pavilion with a curved tiled roof, stone lanterns, a rock waterfall at one bank, distant mountains, a pier.

== 4. Vegetation and pond life ==
Instanced leaf cards with wind and translucency. Trees: weeping cherry (shidare-zakura, pink, sheds petals), cherry blossom, a red Japanese maple, pines and broadleaf background trees, a bamboo grove (Phyllostachys: segmented culms, nodes, drooping leaves), hedges and mounds. Beds: iris clumps, sacred lotus (hasu: cupped petals, seed pod, raised leaves), water lilies with floating pads (FLOAT), spider lily, hydrangea, ferns, moss. Falling sakura petals that land and float on the surface. Pond life: a frog on a lily pad that leaps on click (parabolic hop, splash, croak), a yellow-bellied slider turtle sunning on a rock (procedural shell, wet sheen), dragonflies (shiokara-tombo, aki-akane) that hover and dart, underwater weed and stems, air bubbles on big movements.

== 5. Water ==
Heightfield ripple simulation (256^2, damped wave equation) driven by clicks, drops, fish wakes, the frog and rain; plus 4 Gerstner waves with lengths [2.9, 1.6, 0.85, 0.42] m, amplitudes [0.016, 0.011, 0.007, 0.004] * (0.3 + wind*1.4), directions from the wind direction + offsets [0, 0.45, -0.5, 0.95] rad; a detail normal texture and gust 'cat's paws'. Two passes each frame: a planar reflection with a mirrored camera and a clip plane (half res, mipmapped; koi excluded above water), and a refraction pass of the far side at FULL resolution with 2x MSAA and a depth texture. Surface shader above water: Schlick Fresnel F0=0.02; reflection blurred by local ripple roughness and smeared vertically; refraction displaced by ONE continuous offset = view-space normal * 0.04 * a depth factor averaged over a small ring of 8 depth taps (so it never tears at a koi's outline), with samples that land in front of the surface falling back to the undistorted view; Beer-Lambert along the water path with absorb (0.35, 0.08, 0.04)/clarity and scatter 0.035/clarity, clarity default 1.6 (crystal), in-scatter colour from the sky; shoreline foam where the column is under 5 cm; GGX sun glint (roughness 0.05, soft-shouldered); rain rings; winter ice sheets creeping from the banks with cracks and snow dust. Below water: fine ripples softened, Snell's window via refract() with total internal reflection past 48.6 deg, the above-water render seen through the window, absorption along the path. The camera can dive: crossing the surface swaps layers, adds a low-pass to the audio and an underwater post pass (god rays, particulate, DOF).

== 6. Koi (the centrepiece) ==
One instanced body mesh, one instanced fin mesh, one instanced eye mesh, 20 instances. Body from analytic profile tables (top, bottom, width vs s = 0 nose..1 tail) with Catmull-Rom interpolation: deep rounded back, broad shoulders (width peak 0.10 at s=0.37), blunt head, operculum ridge, eye bulge, protrusible mouth that opens into an O and extends 22 mm, two pairs of barbels, gill covers that breathe. Fins: long dorsal, forked caudal with rounded lobes, anal, large fan-shaped pectorals (length 0.2, width 0.08) and smaller pelvics, all with a ray/membrane texture, folding back when fast and sculling when slow; butterfly (long-fin) variants scale the paired fins ~1.9x and the tail 2x with a billowing veil. Swimming in the vertex shader: lateral spine wave lat(s) = amp*(0.05+0.95 s^2)*sin(5.7 s - phase) + bend*(s-0.3)^2, with normals corrected by the slope. Instance matrix = position, Euler(roll, heading, pitch, 'YZX'), uniform scale = size.

Skin: per-fish pattern atlas 256x128 (R = hi/red field, G = sumi/black field, B = tone, A = belly), low-frequency FBM sampled on the body cylinder; a 512^2 overlapping-cycloid scale normal map (RG normal, B per-scale id, A exposed-rim mask), 4.5x3 repeats; crisp pattern edges scalloped scale by scale (kiwa) at the back of a red patch and a soft blurred sashi edge at the front; sumi granular per scale; pearly white with faint blue-tinted scale pockets; reticulated scale edges for Asagi/Chagoi/Kujaku/Goshiki; lateral line; nostrils, lips, gill slit, pink mouth interior; clearcoat 0.6-1.0, sheen, iridescence 0.25 (0.55-0.6 on metallic varieties); wrap/subsurface warm light past the terminator. Gin Rin: ~35% of scales are tilted mirrors that flash as the fish turns (and still sparkle underwater). Doitsu: scaleless leather skin with rows of large mirror scales beside the dorsal ridge and along the lateral line. Hajiro: white fin tips. Palettes live in an 8xN float texture (base, hi, sumi, belly, fin, fin base, info, flags) so the roster can grow.

Roster (variety, size class; S ~0.21-0.29 m, M ~0.38-0.50 m, L jumbo ~0.62-0.74 m): Kohaku L; Sanke M; Yamabuki Ogon L; Showa L (utsuri sumi wraps the flanks + menware head stripe, hajiro); Orenji Ogon M gin rin; Karasugoi M (black, hajiro); Tancho M (single red crown); Bekko S; Sanke S; Asagi M (blue net, red belly and cheeks); Platinum M butterfly; Chagoi L (bronze, negative retic); Shiro Utsuri M; Hi Utsuri S; Kujaku M butterfly (metallic, matsuba net); Doitsu Kohaku M; Goshiki S; Benigoi S (solid red); Ochiba Shigure M; Kohaku S gin rin. Kohaku/Sanke/Doitsu use step patterns: 2-4 separate red patches with clean white windows between. Each fish gets a small hue/saturation/lightness jitter so no two match. Girth = 0.96-1.05 + (size-0.46)*0.5. Juveniles keep to the shallows and beat faster (freq * sqrt(0.46/size)); jumbo koi swim deeper.

Behaviour: boids (separation, alignment, cohesion), rate-limited turning with angular acceleration and a C-bend into turns, burst-and-glide (a few tail beats then a coast; hover episodes with flared pectorals), soft boundary via the sdf gradient, pier/rock/turtle avoidance, depth preference bounded by the floor, occasional surfacing that leaves drops, wakes near the surface, slow mouth gulps, eye saccades, curious inspection of a submerged camera. The whole fish always stays below the lowest wave trough (depth cap) so the surface never slices it. Hard overlap resolution with three spheres per spine. Koi do NOT cast into the shadow map; instead every underwater fragment computes an analytic soft shadow per fish by walking up the refracted sun ray to the fish's depth and testing a swimming-spine silhouette (penumbra 0.012 + 0.05*h, strength 0.8*exp(-0.2 h), never self-shadowing, also dims 35% of the skylight).

== 7. Interactions ==
Click the water: ripple ring + splash particles + splash sound. Click the frog: it leaps. E / 'Feed the koi': a first-person hand reaches in from the lower right (SkinnedMesh: forearm, palm, five fingers with three bones each, skin textures with knuckle creases, nails, veins; a sleeve), rubs pellets from between thumb and fingers (up to 70 floating pellets that drift, get nudged and are eaten with a gulp and a splash), fish react with a distance-based delay, jostle, snap at the surface, expel gill bubbles; the hand's reach/withdraw use smootherstep easing and a critically damped follow spring in camera space. G / 'Stroke a koi': the camera leans over the bank, a calm medium-sized koi (0.36-0.66 m) glides in, lies alongside with its back just under the surface, lays its dorsal fin flat; the hand approaches from the shoulder, strokes nose-to-tail three times (2.4 s each), the fish rolls into the hand, then the hand withdraws; the user can drag to stroke. Hand collision: sample spheres along the hand are resolved every frame against every koi (in the fish's local frame), the terrain height, rocks (raycast) and lily pads (pushed aside), up to 4 iterations with a 1 mm margin and a filtered lift (fast rise, slow settle). Verify: 0.0 mm penetration, hand peak acceleration under ~8 m/s^2.

== 8. Camera ==
Modes: Cinematic (default), Manual (drag to look, WASD, Q/Space down/up, Shift faster, wheel sets speed), Follow koi (K cycles fish, classic top-down). Cinematic is a directed film tour with letterbox bars, serif captions and dips to black, in this order and duration: The garden from above (13 s, aerial), The koi pond (11 s), Koi (11 s, follows the highest fish), Sacred lotus (10 s), Bamboo grove (12 s), Weeping cherry (10 s), Cherry blossom (11 s), Pond frog (10 s), Yellow-bellied slider (9 s, follow), Beneath the surface (13 s, underwater), back to the pond view (11 s), then loop. Options: hold shot (P), freeze time (O), path speed, stay above water, change season each loop. Physical lens: DOF with GPU autofocus on what is under the crosshair, aperture default f/8 (whole garden sharp), max bokeh size, lens sharpening 0.35; no stair-stepped DOF.

== 9. Weather / seasons (T cycles; GUI dropdown) ==
Presets, each cross-faded over a few seconds:
Sunny: tod 10.5, cloud 0.55, turbidity 2, fog 0.004 (0.5, 0.58, 0.68), wind 0.35, exposure 0.9, grade (1.035, 1, 0.955).
Rain: tod 13, cloud 1, turb 6, overcast 0.85, sun x0.1, hemi x2.1, fog 0.02 (0.2, 0.225, 0.25), rain 1, wet 1, wind 0.55, exposure 1.15; falling rain streaks, rings on the water, wet dark surfaces with puddle sheen, muffled sky.
Autumn: tod 15.7, cloud 0.42, turb 4.5, fog 0.013 (0.62, 0.52, 0.4), autumn 1 (deciduous foliage turns red/orange and thins), wind 0.45, grade (1.07, 1, 0.9).
Winter: tod 11.5, cloud 0.95, overcast 0.7, sun x0.3, hemi x1.9, fog 0.024 (0.56, 0.6, 0.66), snow falling, snow cover 1 on up-facing surfaces, ice sheets from the banks, autumn 0.75 (bare trees), koi sluggish, wind 0.2.

== 10. Post-processing ==
Main HDR -> SSAO (half res, 12-sample normal-oriented hemisphere, blurred) -> bloom (prefilter, threshold 0.9, 5-level mip chain, strength 0.3) -> god rays + DOF when submerged -> composite: exposure, ACES, per-weather colour grade, vignette 0.32, film grain 0.01, lens effects, letterbox. Quality High/Low with automatic drop: first scale resolution smoothly 1.0 -> 0.6 when frame time stays over 22 ms, then switch to Low; recover when fast.

== 11. Audio (Web Audio, all procedural; starts on the first click/key) ==
Master chain: sources -> dry + convolver reverb -> underwater low-pass (420 Hz when submerged, 18 kHz above) -> master gain (volume 0.7). Loops from generated brown/pink/white noise: water lapping (rises with wind and feeding excitement), leaf rustle (wind * gust), waterfall (distance-attenuated), rain, underwater rumble. Events: plip (pellet lands), gulp, splash (scaled by size), frog croak (sawtooth through two bandpasses with AM), frog landing thud, feed-start rattle, dragonfly wing buzz, turtle plop, occasional bird calls, drips, and a shishi-odoshi bamboo knock every 12-30 s. M mutes/unmutes; a Sound switch in the panel mirrors it.

== 12. UI ==
Frosted-glass design system (backdrop blur 20 px + saturate, hairline borders, a soft sheen, one warm accent #f0894c). Bottom-right toolbar dock of icon buttons: camera mode, hold shot, freeze time, clean view, weather, sound, then Stroke a koi and a warm primary Feed the koi; labels collapse on narrow screens, a centred icon dock on phones. Top-right dat.gui restyled as a glass sheet (thin sliders with knobs, pill toggles, glass dropdowns, folder chevrons, a sticky Close bar, never covering the toolbar) with folders: Environment (weather, time, azimuth, wind, wind direction), Water (clarity, wave height, caustics), Koi (fish count 0-20, feed), Rendering (quality, auto-drop, exposure, bloom, bloom threshold, SSAO, god rays, grain, vignette, sharpening), Lens (DOF, f-stop, max bokeh), Camera (film tour, letterbox, change season each loop, mode, follow, path speed, stay above, hold, freeze, clean view, volume, sound), Close-ups. Top-left: an fps/ms HUD and a Guide card listing every shortcut with key chips; I or its x hides it, a small ? brings it back. Shortcuts: C camera mode, P hold, O freeze, V clean view (Esc exits), E feed, G stroke, K follow, T weather, M mute, H panel, I guide. Mute and guide state persist in localStorage. A loader with a progress bar while the world builds. A toast for transient messages.

== 13. Verification targets (do these before calling it done) ==
- Screenshots: aerial, pond level, koi close-up top-down, underwater, each weather; every koi variety lined up in sunlight.
- Native-resolution crops of a koi's outline through the water: no doubled/ghost outline, no stair-steps.
- Hand: 0.0 mm penetration into koi/rocks/terrain during feed and stroke; peak on-screen acceleration under ~8 m/s^2; no NaN in any fish state.
- Performance on a 2x display: High 50-90 fps, Low 100+ fps.
- Every shader compiles with no console errors; the full script parses.

title: Vox-Style Water to Steam Explainer
author: AIUnderTheHood-c7w
prompt:
Act as a senior motion designer and creative programmer. Write the code to generate a clean, educational 10-second motion graphics video explaining how water turns to steam. The style must mimic a Vox explanatory video: minimalist, editorial, highly legible, and driven by smooth geometric transitions.

Technical Specifications:
- Duration: 10 seconds
- Framerate: 30 fps
- Background Color: Pale Cream (#F7F4EF)
- Primary Typography: Dark Charcoal (#1A1A1A) for clean, geometric sans-serif labels
- Accent Colors: Deep Blue (#2E5B88) for water, Bright Terracotta (#D95D39) for heat/energy

Storyboard & Animation Breakdown:
- Scene 1 (0:00 - 0:03) | The Liquid State:
  Fill the bottom third of the frame with a smooth, perfectly looping 2D sine wave representing calm blue water. Add 4-5 tightly packed, neatly arranged circular "H2O molecules" inside the liquid. They should gently jitter or vibrate slightly to simulate liquid molecules. Add a clean text label at the top reading: "Liquid: Molecules are bound closely."

- Scene 2 (0:03 - 0:06) | Thermal Energy:
  A subtle, warm terracotta gradient or wave rises from the bottom of the frame to signify heat. As the heat rises, accelerate the jittering speed of the circular molecules dramatically. The text smoothly transitions (using a crisp fade and slide-up) to: "Heat increases kinetic energy."

- Scene 3 (0:06 - 0:10) | Phase Change (Steam):
  The bounds of the liquid break. The circular molecules suddenly burst outward, flying upward into the top two-thirds of the screen, spreading far apart from one another. Fade out the liquid sine wave. The molecules should float freely and rapidly bounce off the edges of the frame like gas particles. Change the main text label to: "Gas: Bonds break into steam."

Animation Mechanics:
- Use clean math and smooth easing curves (cubic-bezier or easeInOut) for all structural transitions.
- Ensure all particle movements feel fluid, organic, and physically reactive, rather than rigid or linear.
- Output the complete, functional, and self-contained code (e.g., HTML/Canvas, SVG/CSS, or Processing/Python) so I can preview the entire 10-second sequence immediately.

Then render it at 1920x1080 with a headless browser and FFmpeg, and save it as steam1.mp4.

title: Pip the Robot Coded Anime Short
author: denden_zatsugaku
prompt:
あなたは、コードだけで作る45〜50秒のアニメーション短編の、監督・アニメーター・リガー・コンポジター・サウンドデザイナー・レンダリングエンジニアです。制作基準は「本物のアニメーションスタジオの短編に見え、X（Twitter）で拡散されるレベル」。これを複数段階の制作プロセスとして扱ってください。最終レンダリングを急がないこと。マイルストーンごとに進め、静止画を何度も書き出してよく見て、正直に批評して直してください。
■ 一言で言うと
Pipは、廃材から作られた、小さくて好奇心いっぱいのロボット。自分の世界を楽しく走り回っていると、周りの世界が作り直され（再生成され）始める。やがて彼は、誰かがPromptで自分の現実を操っていることに気づく。Promptはどんどんばかげていき、最後に彼は宙に浮かぶPrompt入力欄によじ登って「let me out（ここから出して）」と打ち込む。するとカメラが引き、彼の宇宙はすべて、散らかった作業台に立てかけられたスマホで再生されている動画だったと分かる。そしてそれを見ているのは、もう1体のPip。彼もまさにPromptに操られようとしている。完璧なループ。
笑いはすべてセリフなしで成立させること。Pipは目、アンテナ、体の動き、小さなロボットの鳴き声だけで伝える。3〜5秒ごとに必ず新しい見どころ（笑い・驚き）を入れる。
■ キャラクター設定（譲れない点）
コードを書く前に、添付したキャラクターシート画像をよく見てください。自分の言葉で詳しく説明し、分かったことを docs/character_bible.md に書くこと。
- 大きさ：身長およそ28cm。とても小さい。作品全体でこの小ささを感じさせること。
- 頭：幅の広いクリーム色の角丸ヘルメット。柔らかい黄色の縁取りがあり、黒く艶のあるバイザー（画面）を囲む。目はその画面に表示される：暖かいクリーム色に光る大きな2つの目、濃い瞳、明るいハイライト。両側に小さなグラファイト色の耳当て。縁には擦り傷、引っかき傷、灰褐色の汚れ。
- アンテナ：頭の右上から伸びる細いグラファイト色の棒と、小さな濃いオレンジ色の信号旗。これが彼の「しっぽ」：感情に合わせて立ち、垂れ、くねり、震える。
- 体：箱型のクリーム色の胴体。黄色の縁取り、警告の三角マーク、リベット、汚れ。胸に小さな扉があり、開くと柔らかく光る小さな緑の芽が見える。背面：パネル、通気グリル、オレンジのパネル、小さな葉のデカール。
- 側面のデカール：「PIP」の文字とオレンジの斜めストライプ。
- 腕：細い分節のグラファイト色の腕。黄色の関節カバーと3本指の爪。とても表情豊か。
- 車輪：太いゴムの車輪が4つ。黄色のハブ、独立懸架。頑丈でコンパクト。
- 性格：好奇心旺盛、優しい、根性がある、表情豊か、いつも探検している。「小さなロボット、大きな感情」。怒っていても意地悪にはならない。怒りもかわいく、意志が強い。
- 配色：キャラクターシートの色見本から正確な配色を抽出し（Python/PILで画像をサンプリング）、src/theme/palette.ts に保存する：クリーム（体）、柔らかい黄色（主調）、濃いオレンジ（アクセント）、グラファイト（金属・機械部品）、灰褐色（摩耗・汚れ）、ミントブルー（光・UI）。
アイデンティティ固定ルール：どの世界でも、ヘルメットとバイザーのシルエット、アンテナの旗、黄色の縁取り、爪の腕、4つの車輪が一目で分かること。世界が変えるのは描き方だけで、デザインは決して変えない。唯一の意図的なデザイン変化は第3幕の「もっと可愛く」のギャグだが、そこでもヘルメットの形、アンテナ、車輪は変えない。
■ 技術スタック
- Remotion（React + TypeScript）で、フレーム単位で正確かつ決定的にレンダリングする。出力は1920×1080、30fps、H.264、高ビットレート（CRF 14前後）。横長。
- キャラクターのリグと大部分の絵はSVGで作る。パーティクル、水、爆発、発光、ノイズなどが必要なときだけCanvas/WebGL（@remotion/three または素のcanvas）を使う。
- 画風の「質感」、傷、汚れには、SVGフィルタ（feTurbulence、feDisplacementMap、feMorphology、feGaussianBlur）と自作のcanvasシェーダーを使う。
- 速い動きには @remotion/motion-blur（または自作のサブフレーム合成）でモーションブラーをかける。
- 配色抽出、音声の合成、QA用コンタクトシートの生成にはPython（numpy/scipy/PIL）を使う。音声の結合、ループ確認、コンタクトシートにはffmpegを使う。
- すべてシード付きで決定的にする。シードなしの Math.random() は禁止。
- 外部の著作物素材は一切使わない。実在のブランドのロゴや製品名も出さない。Prompt入力欄のUIは汎用的なオリジナルデザインにする。フォントはGoogle Fontsのみ（例：UIはInter、手書きメモは丸みのある手書きフォント）。
- 想定マシン：MacBook Pro M4、メモリ24GB。レンダリングの並列数は無理のない範囲にする。
■ キャラクターリグ（最初に作る。作品の核）
src/character/ を、きちんとした2Dカットアウトのリグとして作る。
- 階層：root → 車台（サスペンション付き）→ 胴体 → 首の関節 → 頭（ヘルメット + バイザー + 耳当て）→ アンテナ → 旗。胴体 → 肩 → 上腕 → 前腕 → 爪（差し替え可能な爪のポーズ：開く、閉じる、つまむ、指さす、突く／打つ、縁をつかむ、手を振る）。車台 → 4つの車輪。車輪はそれぞれ独自のサスペンションばねを持ち、回転は移動距離から決める。
- バイザーの顔システム（いちばん重要）：目は黒い画面に描かれた形なので、完全にプロシージャルな顔として扱う。目の大きさ、丸み、上まぶた・下まぶたの切り欠き、瞳の大きさと位置、ハイライトの位置、発光の強さ、つぶし／伸ばし、特殊な形（きらめく星、^ ^ の笑顔の弧、無表情の平らな線、渦巻き、小さなハート）をパラメータで制御する。目にはうっすら走査線と画面の反射を入れ、画面らしく見せる。まばたきは3〜4フレームで目を縦につぶして表現する。
- 表情：キャラクターシートの6つの表情に正確に合わせる：好奇心（「?」が出る）、照れ（目線を下にそらす、頬の赤み）、興奮（笑顔の弧の目と小さな放射線）、心配（小さな目、汗のしずく）、決意（上まぶたを斜めに切る）、大喜び（星の目とハートが出る）。さらに追加する：カメラを真顔で見つめる（半目の平らな目、アンテナがだらんと垂れる）、恐怖（震える小さな瞳、見開いた目）、怒っているけどかわいい（決意 + 画面がオレンジに明滅）、そして3段階の「変身（グローアップ）」（第3幕参照）。
- 二次的な動き（フォロースルー）：減衰ばねで動くアンテナと旗（これが主な表現手段なので常に使う）、止まるたび・段差のたびのサスペンションの弾み、腕の揺れ、加速・ブレーキ時の頭のわずかな遅れ、車輪が巻き上げるほこり。
- ターンアラウンド：キャラクターシートに合わせた正面・3/4・側面・背面。向きが変わるときはきれいにビューを切り替える。
- ループアニメ：前進走行（シートにあるスピード線とほこり付き）、待機の揺れ（サスペンションのゆっくりした呼吸 + ときどきアンテナがぴくっ + まばたき）、恐怖で後ずさり、驚いて見上げる、小さな物を持つ、上に手を伸ばす、よじ登る、突いて入力する。
- 胸の扉：開閉をアニメーションでき、芽の柔らかい緑の光があふれる。
- 画風スキンのインターフェース：リグはstyleプロパティを受け取り、形を変えずに、線の太さ、塗り、質感、汚れ、輪郭の揺らぎ（ボイル）、陰影の付け方、フィルタを変えられる。これが、どの世界でも彼が彼であり続ける仕組み。
- マイルストーン1のチェック：「ラインナップ」の静止画を1枚書き出す。4方向のターンアラウンド + 6つの表情のPipを、参考画像と並べる。並べて比較し、参考画像を見た人が誰でも「これはPipだ」と言うまで直す。これを通るまで先に進まない。
■ 世界（画風の質感）
各世界は、手前・中景・奥の視差レイヤーを持つ完全な環境コンポーネントで、Pip専用の画風スキンを持つ。すべての世界がカメラと奥行きの処理を共有できるよう、共通の WorldLayer の仕組みを作る。
比率のルール：カメラはPipの目線に近い低い位置（地面から約20cm）に置く。すべてが巨大に見える。人間は巨大な脚と靴として現れ、縁石は崖、水たまりは湖。これが小さなロボットを映画的に見せる鍵。
- 基本世界：黄金の時間（夕方）の、草木に覆われた街。暖かい夕日、風化した石とレンガ、苔と低い植物、遠くにかすむ高層ビル。絵画的で、温かく、生活感がある。これが「現実」。真相が明かされる場面もこの世界を使う。
- アニメ風の東京：くっきりしたセル塗り、太い輪郭線、架空の（ブランドではない）店名が光る看板、スピード線、巨大なピンクの雪のように舞う桜の花びら。バイザーにはアニメ特有のきらめくハイライト。
- 粘土の村：柔らかく丸い形、指紋やこすった跡のような質感、ストップモーションのような間（Pipは2コマ打ちで描く）、暖かいタングステン光。粘土で作ったように見える。
- 中世の戦場：ぬかるんだ野原、旗、遠くの投石機、煙。鎧を着たブーツが轟音とともに彼の横を通り過ぎる。彼はその中を平然と走り、アンテナが身をかわす。
- ブロックの街：すべてが上面に凸のある汎用のプラスチックブロックでできている（実在ブランドの様式やロゴは使わない）。つやのあるプラスチックのハイライト。Pipもプラスチックの光沢で描かれ、車輪は少し角ばる。
- 水中：海底の街並みに珊瑚の街灯、魚がバイザーの前を泳ぎ、コースティクスの光の模様、噴出孔から泡。アンテナの旗は海藻のようにゆっくり揺れる。
- 鉛筆スケッチ：紙の質感、鉛筆のハッチング、補助線、消しゴムの跡。彼の線はずっと揺らいでいて（ボイル）、毎フレーム描き直されているように見える（キャラクターシート下部のスケッチに合わせる）。
作品を貫く笑いの軸：芽。冒頭で、Pipは小さな緑の芽を片方の爪で大切に持っている（「小さな物を持つ」ポーズ）。芽はどの世界でも生き残り、その世界に合わせて姿を変える：きらめくセル画の芽、粘土の芽、壊れた小さな兜の鉢に植えた芽、ブロックの芽、水中で泡を吐く芽、スケッチの芽。世界が変わるたびに、彼は芽を守る。これが作品の感情の錨。
■ 象徴的な遷移：「再生成（Regeneration）」
世界の切り替えは、普通のワイプではなく、AI画像の再生成のように見えなければならない。RegenTransition コンポーネントを作る：
- 画面が縁から内側へ、漂う拡散モデル風のノイズに溶けていき（最初は彼の体を覆わない）、数フレーム構造化されたノイズを保ち、そこから新しい世界が、粗い色の塊から細部へとノイズを取り除くように浮かび上がる。
- Pipの体は世界より一拍遅れて変わり、一瞬だけ半分が古い画風・半分が新しい画風になってから、新しいスキンに切り替わる。切り替えの瞬間、バイザーに2フレームのグリッチ（走査線の裂け）が入る。この半分だけ切り替わった状態が、彼がずっとそこにいることの視覚的な証拠になる。
- 再生成のたびに、かすかな「シュッ、パチパチ」という音。いくつかの再生成では、Pipが小さく驚いた鳴き声を出す。
- 1回あたり8〜12フレーム。方向とノイズのシードを毎回変え、繰り返しに見えないようにする。
■ 脚本（30fpsで約48秒）
時間は目安。見せ場が少し長いほうが伝わるなら、自分で調整してよい。最初の2秒で必ず観客をつかむこと。
第1幕：いい朝（0:00〜0:03）
基本世界での低い位置からの追従ショット。Pipは苔むした縁の上を左から右へ走り、芽を持ち、好奇心いっぱいの目で、アンテナが上下に揺れる。走行の途中から始める（最後のループのため）。
0:02、最初の再生成が何の前触れもなく起きる。
第2幕：怒涛の変化（0:03〜0:14）
世界が約1.4秒ごとに次々と変わる：アニメ風東京 → 粘土の村 → 中世の戦場 → ブロックの街 → 水中 → 鉛筆スケッチ。
感情の流れ：最初は大喜び（星の目、これは最高だと思っている）、次に好奇心（「?」が出る）、それから心配（汗のしずく、アンテナが垂れる）、最後にスケッチの世界で急ブレーキ。サスペンションが弾み、ブレーキ跡が残る。
カメラは同じ追従の構図に固定し、変わるのは世界だけにして、笑いを分かりやすくする。
第3幕：Prompt（0:14〜0:30）
基本世界に戻る。Pipは驚いて見上げる（キャラクターシートのポーズを参考に）。空に、巨大な浮かぶPrompt入力欄がフェードインする。ミントブルーに光り、ガラスのようで角が丸く、UIは柔らかくオリジナル。点滅するカーソルとともに文字が自動で打たれる：「make it more cinematic（もっと映画っぽくして）」→ Enterキーの音。映画のシネスコの黒帯が一瞬で入り、太陽が大げさになる：巨大なアナモルフィックのレンズフレア、光芒（ゴッドレイ）、オレンジとティールの色調、スローモーションのほこり、ドラマチックな葉が1枚バイザーの前を舞う。彼はまぶしさに目を細める。アンテナの旗が、どこから吹くのか分からない強風の中で英雄的にはためく。
「add explosions（爆発を追加して）」：巨大なカートゥーン調のオレンジの爆発が、破片とともに彼の後ろで次々と起きる。彼は振り返らない。目が平らな半目になる。ゆっくりと頭を回し、カメラをまっすぐ見つめる。真顔。まるまる1秒の間。そして爆発が1つ彼のすぐ近くに落ち、彼はキャラクターシートの「恐怖で後ずさり」ポーズに一瞬で切り替わり、頭の上に「!!」が出て、体で芽をかばう。
「make the protagonist more adorable（主人公をもっと可愛くして）」：変身1段階目：目が大きく明るくなり、頬に赤み、アンテナに小さなリボン。水たまりに映った自分を見て、目がおびえる。
「more.（もっと）」：2段階目：パステル調に塗り直され、目がバイザーいっぱいに広がって3重のハイライト、ハートときらめきが漂い、車輪がふわふわになる。
「MORE.（もっと！）」（大きな文字、画面が揺れる）：3段階目：滑稽なほど極端に可愛い。全身がぬいぐるみのような毛並みに覆われ、巨大なアニメの目、虹のハロー、合唱の「アー」という効果音、ハートの紙吹雪。ヘルメットの形、アンテナ、車輪はそのままなので、彼がPipであることは明らか。そして巨大な可愛い目の中で、彼の本当の目は小さくおびえたまま。ここが笑いどころ。
第4幕：彼がキレる（0:30〜0:38）
Pipが激しく震え、可愛い状態がガラスのように割れて剥がれ落ちる。彼は元に戻り、傷だらけで、ものすごく怒っている（決意の表情、画面がオレンジに明滅）。
彼は胸の扉を開け、芽をそっと中にしまって守る。扉が「カチッ」と閉まる。混乱の中の唯一の静かで優しい瞬間で、とても大切。
彼は前へダッシュし、石から飛び上がり、浮かぶPrompt入力欄の縁を両方の爪でつかみ、体を引き上げる。車輪が縁で空回りする（キャラクターシートの「浮かぶPrompt入力欄に手を伸ばす」ポーズに合わせる）。カメラは彼を追って上にティルトする。
入力欄の上で、彼は片方の爪でバックスペースを押し続ける。古いPromptが速いカチカチ音とともに1文字ずつ消え、消えていく文字が彼のバイザーに映る。
彼は片方の爪で、ゆっくり、一文字ずつ突いて打つ：「let me out」。そして力をため、Enterキーを思いきり叩く。
第5幕：静止と真相（0:38〜0:47）
すべてが止まる：宙に浮いた破片、落ちていく紙吹雪、漂うほこり、入力欄の上でポーズをとるPip。すべての音が切れ、約1秒の完全な静寂。
カメラが滑らかに引き始める。画面の縁に角丸の長方形が現れる：彼の宇宙は、スマホの画面で再生されている動画だった。さらに引く：スマホは欠けたマグカップに立てかけられ、予備部品、配線、ネジ、廃材が散らかった作業台の上にある（「明日の余りもので作られた」）。その前に、巨大なスマホの横で小さく座っているのが、もう1体のPip。同じ傷、同じアンテナで、動画を見ている。
2体目のPipの目がゆっくりまばたきする。アンテナが少し垂れる。かすかで静かな鳴き声。
第6幕：ループ（0:47〜0:50）
2体目のPipの頭上に、同じミントブルーのPrompt入力欄がフェードインし、文字が打たれる：「make it more cinematic.」
彼の目がゆっくり上へ、入力欄のほうへ動く。アンテナの旗が固まる。Enterキーの音とともに、作品の1フレーム目へハードカット。
ループの設計：最後のショットの構図、照明、再生成の始まりによって、1フレーム目に戻るカットが意図的に感じられるようにする。音楽は切り替わりで継ぎ目なくループすること。ffmpegで動画を自分自身とつなげ、継ぎ目を見て確認する。
■ カメラと撮影
- 仮想カメラ：位置、ズーム、回転、手持ちの微振動（シード付きノイズ）、爆発による揺れ、よじ登り時のティルト、真相の場面のドリーアウト。
- 基本はカメラを低くして小ささを強調する。浅い被写界深度：マクロレンズのように、手前の草や小石はぼけ、背景は柔らかく。
- 奥行き：各世界に最低4つの視差レイヤー。大気遠近法（距離に応じてかすみ、彩度を下げる）。
- 速い動き、破片、ジャンプ、よじ登りにはモーションブラーを入れる。
- 各世界のライティング：リグにグラデーションの重ねと乗算の影レイヤーで、キー・フィル・リムの光を作る。バイザーの光は近くの面と彼自身の爪に、かすかに暖かい光を落とす。どの世界でもヘルメットにリムライトを入れる。
- 画面全体のシネマティックな仕上げ：かすかなフィルムグレイン、柔らかいビネット、「映画っぽく」の場面だけごくわずかな色収差。
- 構図：彼を三分割線の上にきちんと置く。ほとんどの人はスマホで見るので、スマホ画面のサイズでも彼の目がはっきり見えること。
■ 文字とタイポグラフィ
- 空のPrompt：すっきりしたUIフォント、小文字、自然な人間のリズムで打つ（一定の速さにしない。短い間を入れ、どこかで一度打ち間違えてバックスペースで直し、リアルさを出す）。
- 文字はスマホで1秒以内に読めること。横幅360ピクセルで確認する。
- 字幕なし、タイトルなし。いきなり始まる。
■ 音（プロシージャルに生成、オリジナル）
すべての音をコードで生成し（Pythonの合成またはオフラインのWeb Audio）、ffmpegでミックスする。
- Pipの声：ピッチベンドするサイン波／FMの音で作ったオリジナルの鳴き声、ビープ、トリル。小さな「感情の語彙」を設計する：好奇心の上がる鳴き声、うれしいトリル、心配の揺れる声、驚いたキュッという声、不機嫌な低いブーン、小さなため息。彼は決して話さない。
- Pipの体の音：腕と頭の動きに合わせたサーボの音、砂利や石の上を転がる車輪のザリザリ音、サスペンションのきしみ、胸の扉の開閉のカチッという音、待機中の柔らかい電気のうなり。
- 音楽：軽やかでループできる温かい曲。世界ごとに楽器編成を変える（アニメは琴／シンセ、粘土は木のマリンバ、中世は太鼓／ホルン、ブロックはプラスチックのカチカチ音、水中はこもったフィルター、スケッチは鉛筆をこするリズム）。
- 効果音：再生成のシュッ・パチパチ、キーボードの打鍵音、Enterキーを叩く「ドン」、低音のある爆発音、合唱の「アー」、ガラスの割れる音、静止の場面の完全な無音、そして真相の場面の静かな作業部屋の環境音（時計のチクタク、遠くの低いうなり）。
- ラウドネスは -14 LUFS 前後に正規化する。後で許諾済みの音源に差し替えられるよう、各ステムを audio/stems/ に置く。
■ 制作ワークフローと自己改善ループ
以下の順に進め、チェックポイントを飛ばさないこと：
1. 計画：docs/character_bible.md、docs/shotlist.md（各ショットのフレーム範囲、カメラ、表情、アンテナの状態、世界、効果音を含む）、docs/style_guide.md を書く。作り始める前に、ショットリストを私に見せること。
2. リグ：Pipを作り、ラインナップ静止画のチェック（上記）を通す。
3. 世界：各世界を、Pipを含む独立した静止画として作る。7つすべてを1枚のコンタクトシートに書き出し、キャラクターが同じに見えるか、比率の感覚があるかを確認する。
4. 遷移：RegenTransition を作り、5秒のテストを書き出す。
5. アニマティック：960×540で作品全体を組み立てる。動きは粗く、音は仮でよい。見て、まずテンポの問題を直す。
6. 本番アニメーションを書き出し、磨く（二次的な動き、イージング、タイミング、アンテナの演技）。最後に仕上げ（ライティング、グレイン、ブラー、汚れ）。
7. 音の処理とミックス。
8. 最終レンダリング。
各ショットについて、この批評ループを最低3回まわすこと：
- npx remotion still でキーフレームの静止画を3〜5枚書き出し、開いてよく見る。
- 次の項目を1〜10点で採点する：Pipが参考画像と一致しているか、目とアンテナから感情が一瞬で読めるか、音なしで笑いが伝わるか、構図、比率の感覚、奥行き、ライティング、仕上げの細かさ、スマホ画面サイズでの読みやすさ。
- 点数と上位3つの問題を docs/review_log.md に書き、直して、書き出し直して、採点し直す。すべての項目が8点以上になるまで続けてから、次に進む。
- 通しのプレビューを書き出すたびに、ffmpegで0.5秒ごとのコンタクトシートを作り、作品全体の流れを1枚で確認する。
批評は正直に。安っぽく見えるところがあれば、そう言って直すこと。よくある失敗：硬くて生気のないアンテナ、転がらずに滑っている車輪、光る画面ではなくシールに見える目、サスペンションの重さがない、どれも同じに見える遷移、読めない文字、キャラクターの比率の崩れ。
■ 納品物
- out/pip_final_1080p.mp4：作品本体。
- out/pip_loop_check.mp4：ループを確認するため、作品を2回続けて再生したもの。
- out/poster_frame.png：X（Twitter）投稿のサムネイル用のベストな1フレーム（おそらく爆発を背に真顔でカメラを見つめるPip）。
- out/lineup.png：すべての世界のPipを並べたラインナップ。
- 構成がはっきりしてコメントの付いたソースコードと、再レンダリングの方法を書いたREADME。
第1段階から始めてください。作り始める前に、必要な質問があれば聞いてください。なければ、自分で思い切った創作上の判断をしてください。

<direction>
Editorial and cinematic, one continuous take through one 3D world. It is never a deck. A perspective camera directs attention with extreme close-ups, 3/4 angles, orbits, crane-ups, a whip, a dive and a fly-through, and there is one subject at a time. The cursor stands for the human's attention and carries continuity. It pulls the brief out of the cold session, carries it to four agents, drops it, clicks the core, types, sweeps, and drags the learning into the dark. Then it vanishes, because Digital Me works while you sleep. It comes back to find Codex already knows, and ends with a click on motusai.co.
Two materials. Outside Digital Me is a paper world with ink objects, and ink type standing in depth. Inside is an ink world with white type. Every region change hides inside a full frame: a dive through the solid black core into black, and a paper iris that floods out of the Digital Me node into white. Nothing cuts visibly.
Type is minimal: one big serif word or line per state, flipped up word by word on its baseline (rotationX -95 to 0), and flipped away the same way. Everything else is real product detail in mono, sitting inside panels.
Spring everywhere. Every move rides a damped spring (snap, slick, cam, whip, soft, bounce). Only typing is linear, and the dive accelerates on p cubed. Motion blur is driven by projected camera velocity. Depth of field blurs only the big words and cloud cards that sit off the focal plane. Panels carry soft long shadows.
Agents appear only as their real icons, in white. Their names are never written.
Banned: flat full-frame surfaces and deck-filling, hard cuts, any color, linear or bouncy UI easing outside the listed springs, and eyebrows and small text of any kind: the "MOTUSAI — DIGITAL ME" folio, "04 / 12" counters, a pinned Apply → Work → Capture index, captions, nameplates, title bars, labels like "Your brief" or "LEARNING CAPTURED →", and the "Open source · MIT · plain files in git" plate. Also banned: agent names as text, placeholder or monogram icons, pure-white page backgrounds, and narration.
</direction>

<build>
1. HyperFrames 0.8.77 project (npx hyperframes init digital-me-24s-cinematic --example=blank --skill=general-video), 1920x1080, 30 fps, 24 s. The film is one index.html generated by tools/build.mjs (node tools/build.mjs). Keep all numbers in that script and emit the HTML, CSS and a DATA JSON from it. Load GSAP 3.14.2 plus TextPlugin from jsdelivr. #root has data-composition-id="main". There is one paused gsap.timeline, and a single linear driver tween (t from 0 to 24) calls frame(t) in onUpdate. Register it with window.__timelines["main"] = tl. frame(t) owns every 3D placement and must be a pure function of t. GSAP animates only inner nodes, for the pops, flips, types, glows and washes.
2. Lens and world: #stage has perspective 1400px with its origin at 960 540. #world is a zero-size preserve-3d node at 960,540, with y down and z toward the viewer. The camera is analytic. Each key is a target point q, angles rx ry rz, and a dolly zc. The world gets translate3d(-M·q + (0,0,zc)) rotateZ rotateX rotateY, where M is that rotation matrix. Each key is a leg {t, d, ease} that springs from the previous value, and d = 0 is a jump that only happens inside full black or white.
3. Springs are the damped-oscillator step response f(t) = 1 - e^(-zwt)(cos wd·t + (zw/wd) sin wd·t), evaluated over progress 0 to 1 and corrected linearly so that f(1) = 1: snap (0.55, 12), slick (0.72, 11), cam (0.9, 9), whip (0.94, 12.5), soft (0.9, 7), bounce (0.45, 13). The note (from 1.5 to 4.0) and the learning card (from 13.5 to 14.1) are placed at fixed offsets from the cursor point, so they travel with the hand.
7. Carousel: panel k sits at ring angle phi + fan[k], blended into its wing pose by the spread value. Beams and constellation links are 1px-wide boxes scaled along X and aimed with rotateY and rotateZ computed from their endpoints.
8. Motion blur: an SVG feGaussianBlur on #lens, a 2D wrapper above the perspective stage. Take the mean screen displacement over 1/30 s of five probes (q, ±320 x, ±240 y), multiply by 0.18 and the leg's blur factor, clamp at 22px, and apply separate x and y deviations only above 1.6px, never on jump frames. Depth of field: every big word and cloud card carries its world point, and gets blur(clamp(|z_cam - zc| × 0.011 - 1.2, 0, 12)px) when that is over 0.3.
9. Regions: the paper-1 set is visible when t < 7.97, the ink set when 7.94 ≤ t < 18.95, and paper-2 when t ≥ 18.88. The rule card's back face shows from 14.86, T2's back from 23.12, T2's front until 23.3, and the iris only from 18.45 to 19.0. The background flips to ink at 7.95 and to paper at 18.9.
10. Audio as HyperFrames audio tags. The bed is on track 10 with data-media-start 0.03, volume 0.7, a lowpass fx-chain, and automation: frequency 20000, then 650 from 18.05 to 18.5, then 20000 by 18.95; volume 1, then 0.8 over the same window, then 0 from 23.55 to 24.0. Put the SFX on tracks 11 and up, as time/duration/volume:
type 0/.4/.45, key .5/.3/.35, whoosh .55/.5/.25, pop 1.5/.5/.35, whoosh 1.58/.55/.5
key 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5 each /.3/.45, whoosh 2.2, 2.7, 3.2 each /.4/.2
whoosh 3.95/.55/.3, pop 4.05/.5/.3, whoosh 4.35/.55/.45, whoosh 5.95/.55/.35, pop 6.1/.5/.4
click 7.0/.3/.5, chime 7.02/1.2/.7, cinematic whoosh 7.2/1.0/.5 (media start 1.95)
click 8.2/.3/.45, type 8.22/.32/.45, pop 8.52/.5/.3, whoosh 9.95/.5/.25, confirm 11.0/.8/.45, click 11.5/.3/.35, whoosh 11.95/.4/.2, shutter 12.5/.6/.45
click 13.5/.3/.45, whoosh 13.56/.55/.35, whoosh 14.25/.5/.3, pop 14.74/.5/.35, whoosh 15.88/.55/.4, pop 16.46/.5/.35, key 16.97/.3/.3, whoosh 18.0/.55/.3
cinematic whoosh 18.2/.9/.35 (media start 2.0), whoosh 20.0/.6/.35, type 20.12/.3/.45, type 20.5/.2/.45, pop 21.0/.5/.3, confirm 21.3/.8/.5
type 22.08/.26/.45, pop 22.52/.5/.3, whoosh 23.0/.5/.35, click 23.5/.3/.5, ending pop 23.5/.18/.6
There is no loudnorm pass. The mix measures -13.4 LUFS integrated with a true peak around -1.6 dBFS.
11. Validate with npx hyperframes check (lint, layout and contrast), then snapshot about 30 frames: npx hyperframes snapshot --at 0.15,0.45,1.3,2.0,... --no-end --describe false --timeout 25000 -o snapshots/v2x. Read the contact sheets. For framing, node tools/build.mjs --probe '{"name":[x,y,z]}' 8.6,10.8 prints projected screen points, which is how the verbs are kept in clear space and inside the frame.
12. Render: npx hyperframes render -o renders/digital-me-24s-cinematic-v2-1080p.mp4 --quality delivery --skill general-video (about 22 s). The result is H.264 High, yuv420p, 1920x1080, 30 fps, about 2.1 Mb/s, with AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo at about 198 kb/s, 24.000 s long. Make the 720p copy with ffmpeg -vf scale=1280:720:flags=lanczos -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart. Then pull 20 frames from the MP4 into a contact sheet and check them.
</build>

<gotchas>
Region visibility set with GSAP tl.set was wrong after out-of-order seeks in Studio and in the renderer. Compute every visibility window inside frame(t) from t alone.
Never let GSAP and frame() write the same element. Wrappers with class .obj are placed by frame() or by a static transform, and GSAP only touches their children.
Don't read offsetWidth inside frame(). Give cursor followers fixed sizes (520x170 and 700x160).
hyperframes check flags intentionally layered text (stacked pastes, note lines, card text) as content_overlap errors. Put data-layout-allow-overlap on each text element, not only on the wrapper, and allow overflow, overlap and occlusion on #world. The composition_file_too_large warning is accepted for a single take. The contrast audit sees 0 texts in 3D, so judge contrast by eye.
The first dive, on a whip spring, overshot and landed on grey. Accelerate on p cubed, fade the core name, and cover 7.85 to 7.96 with a full ink veil before switching regions. Do camera jumps only inside that black and inside the paper iris.
Flip cards need backface-visibility hidden plus explicit visibility windows for each face, or both faces bleed through.
Motion blur goes on a 2D wrapper above the perspective stage, never on the preserve-3d world. Depth-of-field blur goes only on leaf elements.
hyperframes render has no 720p preset (presets only scale up). Render 1080p and downscale.
Live Studio playback stutters on the blur-heavy moments (the whips, the dive, the cloud). Judge timing from snapshots or a render.
The 720p file measured a true peak of -0.7 dBTP, slightly hot. Pull the bed down 0.5 dB if the platform re-encodes.
The agent marks belong to Anthropic, OpenAI, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw. Use them only to identify supported agents, and use their official files. This film recolored them to monochrome to hold the black-and-white palette, so check each brand's guidelines before shipping. The fonts are OFL. The bed is under HeyGen's sounds-library license, and the SFX are the HyperFrames bundled set plus MotusAI's own files.
</gotchas>

<start>
Confirm you have the four icon SVGs, the three fonts, the lockup, bgm_001.wav and the SFX, and ask me for anything missing. Then write tools/build.mjs with the anchors and the camera and cursor keys above. Generate index.html, run hyperframes check, and show me a contact sheet of about 30 frames (at least one per beat-event cluster, including 7.7 to 7.97 for the dive and 18.3 to 18.9 for the iris) before rendering. Render only after I approve the preview.
</start>

Core Motion Graphics DNA (Apply to Final Output)

   * Living Components: Animate sweeping radar beams, SVG bezier workflow lines (stroke-dashoffset with glowing traveling pulses), iPhone Dynamic Island expansions with live green audio bars, and cascading iMessage/Slack-style chat threads.
4. Dynamic Background Shifts:
   * Shift the canvas mood across acts (e.g., start on crisp white/mesh gradient for the hook, flash to electric lime or deep dark mode #0A0A0A for the core workflow, and resolve on a glowing dark or signature brand-color outro).
Time-Pacing Blueprints
Scale the scene count dynamically to match the user's chosen duration:

title: Three.js Halloween Haunted Dark Ride
author: silverchipmunk
prompt:
Build a Halloween haunted dark ride in Three.js: a first-person, on-rails experience that feels like a real theme park attraction, not a generic spooky level.

WHAT A DARK RIDE ACTUALLY IS (follow this closely):
- The rider sits in a small 2-seat car on a hidden track. The camera is locked to the car with slight sway, bumps on track joints, and limited mouse-look (~60° each way).
- The building is mostly PITCH BLACK. You never see walls, ceilings, or the full room. Only staged "show scenes" are lit, each a small vignette lit by tight spotlights, surrounded by black.
- Show scenes are separated by black curtains, swinging doors, and tight turns, so each one is a reveal.
- It is theatrical and handmade: painted plywood flats, forced-perspective backdrops, fiberglass monster figures with a slightly glossy, stiff look, fake cobwebs, rubber bats on wires. It should look built by a theme park crew, not realistic.
- Signature effects: UV blacklight with fluorescent-painted props glowing neon green, orange, magenta, and cyan; strobe flashes; fog at floor level; pop-up scares that jolt forward when the car passes; animatronics with looping, slightly jerky motion.

RIDE SEQUENCE (about 2.5 minutes):
1. Outdoor load station at night: orange string lights, a carved-pumpkin facade, a few NPC riders boarding the cars ahead of you, and a ride operator. The car rolls through doors into darkness.
2. Haunted parlor: a slow section with a dusty dining table, ghost figures (Pepper's ghost style: transparent and glowing), and portraits whose eyes follow you.
3. Blacklight graveyard: everything glows fluorescent, tombstones are painted flats, and skeleton animatronics pop out of graves.
4. Total darkness: a few seconds of near black, sounds only, and one strobe reveals a monster mannequin inches from the car.
5. Mad lab: green chemical glow, sparking Tesla coils, and a creature strapped to a table that lurches.
6. SPEED SECTION: the car accelerates hard through a twisting tunnel with flickering red lights, rushing past dozens of monster mannequins lining the walls, plus a short drop.
7. Mirror or spinning-tunnel room with colorful rotating lights.
8. Finale: a giant monster face over the exit doors, a last scare, then you roll back out into the station lights.

The NPC riders in the cars ahead should be visible in silhouette sometimes, reacting by raising their arms on the fast part.

ART AND TEXTURES:
- Make procedural or canvas-generated textures for painted wood flats (visible brush strokes and edge wear), peeling wallpaper, stone, fabric curtains, and fluorescent paint.
- Monster mannequins should be stylized and readable from a moving car: exaggerated silhouettes, bold colors, glowing eyes.
- Use emissive materials and bloom for blacklight elements. Keep the global ambient light near zero.
- Fog and volumetric-looking light cones from spotlights are essential.

TECH:
- Use a CatmullRom spline track with per-segment speed control and smooth acceleration.
- Use a trigger system along the track for scares, animatronics, and lights.
- Hold 60 FPS. Use instancing for repeated props and pool lights instead of adding hundreds.
- Add spatial audio hooks per scene: creaks, screams, organ music, track clatter.

QUALITY CHECK: Take screenshots at each scene and ask yourself whether it looks like a real theme park haunted ride or a random dark 3D room. If it is the latter, add more contrast, more theatrical lighting, and more handmade-prop character.

あとはレンダリングしてmp4にしてと伝えて完成。

Each change lands with a squash and stretch over 9 frames (8% wider, 10% shorter, then back). Idle: 0.5 degree sway and a 0.6% breathing scale.
Script: a hook question in the first 4 seconds, a title line, 4 to 5 beats that each carry one visual idea, a one-line payoff. Short sentences, plain words, every claim accurate, no medical advice.
Timing: run silencedetect on my voiceover at -35dB, 0.22s. Cut scenes in the middle of the long pauses and fire every pop, label and pose change on the word it belongs to.
Palette: backgrounds pale blue #D3DFEC, mid blue #B4C7E6, strong blue #6790CB. Outlines and text navy #24364F. Accents amber #F4B740, coral #EE7B5B, teal #58B7A8, lilac #9A86D6. Flat fills only, 5-9px navy outlines on every drawn object.
Scenes: the title card is solid #37557F with two lines of white text sliding in from opposite sides and an amber underline. At least two close-up scenes with no character. One circular zoom bubble, 320px radius, white ring with navy edges, that the character points at. The final scene is #6790CB with 14 lighter rotating rays.
Diagrams: every explainer visual is drawn in code from circles, rounded rectangles and lines: chains of beads joined by a thick navy link, cells with a dotted membrane, arrows as moving dashed lines, labels in white rounded pills with a 6px navy outline.
Captions: Inter ExtraBold Italic, all capitals, 66px, navy, centred at the top between y=200 and y=340, two lines maximum, each line rising 24px and fading in over 9 frames on its word. White with a navy stroke on the strong blue scene.
Movement: a slow push-in from 100% to 104% across every scene, 14 soft white particles drifting upward at 35% opacity, every new element popping in with an 18% overshoot, beads rippling in a wave, a 7% zoom punch on the final line.
Draw order: background, particles, floor line, diagrams, character, captions on top.
Sound: my voiceover at full level. Effects at half the voice level: a swoosh 0.12s before each cut, a whip on each pose change, a pop on each element, a click or chime on key moments, a low hit on the title card and the final line.
Before the full render: render 14 still frames at the busiest moments, look at them, fix overlaps and text leaving the frame.
Banned: gradients, drop shadows, glow, 3D, AI images or AI video, stock footage, music, emojis, watermarks, any character other than the attached one, any other channel's characters, logo or name, text smaller than 30px, a character that floats above the bottom edge, more than two caption lines.
</direction>

title: Fossil Dig to Living T-Rex
author: Ayu_AI_0912
prompt:
【題材：〇〇（生き物の名前）】
のCADデータと、それを元にしたBlender動画を作って。

■ 題材の設定
- 種類・時代・産地：【例：白亜紀後期・北アメリカ／ジュラ紀・ヨーロッパ／現生のシロナガスクジラ】
- 大きさ：【例：全長 約12m、腰の高さ 約4m】（空欄なら一般的な成体の値で）
- 姿勢・復元の考え方：【例：尾を水平にした前傾の二足歩行／四足歩行／泳ぐ姿】
- 一般的な復元イメージであり、特定の標本の実測図ではないと特記事項に書く

■ CADデータ
- DXFで3枚（単位mm、A2、表題欄つき）
  - 発掘区画図（1m方眼の区画に、出土した骨の配置と標本番号）
  - 全身骨格図（側面、骨の名称・全長・高さの寸法）
  - 三面図（側面・正面・上面）と、特徴的な部位の拡大図【例：頭骨／翼／ヒレ】
- 3Dモデル（OBJ/STL/3D DXF）は不要

■ 動画（Blender 4.2、1920×1080、24fps、約20秒）
1. 冒頭：調査用の方眼紙が上から広がり、インクで描かれた発掘区画図が現れる（題字の札・調査印・鉛筆のメモつき）
2. 図面の骨の輪郭が光の線として立ち上がり、化石が「発掘されたときの姿勢」で紙の上に現れる
3. 化石が一本ずつ飛び上がり、立った骨格に組み上がる（体の中心 → 背骨 → 脚 → 肋骨 → 尾 → 首 → 頭 の順など、題材に合わせて）
4. 筋肉が付く → 皮膚（または羽毛・鱗・毛）が覆う。境目が光の帯で進む
5. 方眼紙が消え、周りが【環境：例 白亜紀の森と朝もや／ジュラ紀の湖畔／氷河期の雪原／海の中】だとわかる演出
6. 目が開いてまばたきし、【動き：例 歩き出して吠える／翼を広げて飛び立つ／泳ぎ出す】
7. 最後にタイトル【題材名／英名・学名／ひとことの副題】を表示
8. 本編のあと、ロゴのエンドカード（黒地に柔らかく現れ、光の筋が走ってフェードアウト）

■ カメラ
- 組み上がる間は骨格に寄る（頭・歯・関節をなめるように回る）
- 景色が現れるところで引きの全景へ
- 最後は【例：低い位置から見上げて顔のアップ】

■ 描写（リアル寄り）
- 骨は化石らしい質感（石化した色、ひび、補修の跡）
- 筋肉は繊維の筋、皮膚は【例：大きさの違う鱗、背は暗く腹は明るい色分け】
- 動きは重さが感じられるように（一歩ごとに体が沈む、尾や首で釣り合いを取る）
- 植物は葉の一枚一枚が見える作りに（球の塊にしない）。遠景は木を密に、空気遠近の霞
- 時間帯は【例：朝の低い日差し】、影を長く
- テクスチャはプロシージャルで
- 外観の参考画像：【画像を添付】（なければ一般的な復元イメージで）

■ 音
- 外部素材なしでPython合成
- 紙のすれる音、骨がはまる音、心臓の鼓動が始まる、環境音、足音（または羽ばたき・水音）、鳴き声
- 題材の時代や雰囲気に合ったBGM。ロゴのエンドカードにも音をつける
- 冒頭は1秒カットしてテンポよく

■ PCの負荷
- 最初から軽い設定で描く（見た目が変わらない範囲でサンプル数を下げる）
- 低い優先度で、Blenderは1本ずつ。少しずつ描いて冷ましながら進める
- 本番レンダリングの前に、かかる時間を教えて

■ 進め方
- テスト静止画を確認してから本番レンダリング
- 完成したらMP4で送って

title: Beat-Synced Product Launch Promo
author: 0xAiky
prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for: the product name and a one-line promise, 3 to 5 UI moments to show, one accent color, 10 to 20 real vertical clips I own, and a royalty-free song with a clear drop (e.g. Mixkit, free for commercial use).
</inputs>

<direction>
High-end minimal. One idea per shot, plenty of empty space, one accent color, one clean sans (Geist or Inter) with tight tracking.
Masked type reveals, match cuts, one consistent camera language.
Real footage only, never placeholder cards. No full stops in on-screen text.
Banned: shockwave rings, particle bursts, RGB split, camera shake, lens flares, neon glows, grid floors, flashing backgrounds, bouncy easing.
</direction>

<structure>
10 bars at 120 BPM, 2 seconds each.
Bar 1: the hook appears word by word on the beats.
Bar 2: one hook word morphs into the product UI. A cursor types and clicks.
The drop: a circle expands out of the button into a dark scene.
Then one move per bar:
a wall of real clips with a scan line and 3 winners
the key output revealed as big type
a 3D carousel of real videos with floor reflections and a motion-blurred whip onto one hero clip
the hero inside a phone next to a panel that flips into results
big stats on push cuts
a 3-word ticker
a logo reveal
a fade to black
</structure>

<build>
One HTML file at 1920x1080. Every style is calculated from time inside window.seek(t): no CSS animations, no timers, no state between frames.
Real video: extract clips into 30fps JPEG sequences with ffmpeg and swap img sources per frame. seek awaits the image decodes.
Analyze the song with numpy: tempo, beat grid, energy per bar, and the drop. Calibrate the grid to the actual kick hits. Every cut lands on a downbeat, every UI hit on a beat.
Render with Playwright: 3 subframes per frame at t minus, at, and plus 1/240s, then blend with ffmpeg tmix for real motion blur at 60fps.
Place every sound effect so its measured peak, not its file start, lands on the event. Keep the effects quiet beneath the music. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
Check 20 or more frames before the full render. Fix anything cluttered, overlapping, or difficult to read.

</build>

<gotchas>
Never set opacity or filter on a preserve-3d element, because it flattens and both faces become visible.
Fade its wrapper instead.
Measure element positions at runtime for accurate match cuts.
Only use music and sound effects with licenses that allow commercial use.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me a storyboard with every timing mapped to the beat grid before writing any code.
</start>

title: Lip-Synced Two-Character Dialogue Cartoons
author: mhmazur
prompt:
How to make a short AI dialogue cartoon with Claude Code or Codex:

You need:
- An ElevenLabs API key with Text to Speech + Voices: Read
- An OpenAI key (gpt-image) for the art
- Optional: an OpenRouter key so Gemini can listen to and check the audio
- ffmpeg, Node, Python, Chrome

Save your keys in files (e.g. ~/.config/elevenlabs/api-key), open Claude Code or Codex in an empty folder (in Codex, allow network access), and paste:

Make me one ~30 second animated dialogue video (1920x1080 MP4).

Characters: [your choice]
Situation: [your choice]
Art style: [your choice]

Write a funny 6-8 line back-and-forth with a punchline. Keys are in ~/.config/*/api-key; never print them.

1. Voices: search the ElevenLabs voice library, audition 3-4 voices per character on a real line, and have Gemini (via OpenRouter) pick the best fit.
2. Speech: eleven_v3 with-timestamps, one request per line, with an acting tag like [exasperated]. Use curl.
3. Audio: trim lines using both the timestamps and the waveform (so nothing is clipped and there's no dead air), fit to 30s, add quiet ambience, and compute a per-frame loudness envelope per character.
4. Art: one 16:9 scene with both characters facing each other, mouths closed. Then one edit per character: "change ONLY their mouth to open mid-word."
5. Mouths: diff each edit against the scene to cut out a feathered mouth overlay.
6. Render: canvas page + Puppeteer + ffmpeg. Show a mouth overlay when that character is loud. Word-synced captions styled to match the art. One fixed shot, both characters always visible, no camera moves, and no black first frame.
7. QA: have Gemini check the audio against the script, fix issues, and check test stills before the full render.

Keep all working files in a source/ folder so it can be re-rendered later.

title: VibeVoice Speech Recognition Promo
author: HaileyAILabs
prompt:
VibeVoice｜40 秒高质量创意种草视频制作

请参考我上传的分镜图，为微软开源项目 VibeVoice 制作一支 40 秒的高质量创意种草视频。

一、创作目标

我要的不是普通的科技产品介绍，也不是把 GitHub README 做成 PPT 动画。

而是一支视觉审美出色、镜头富有创意、动画流畅、音乐节奏强烈，同时能让观众直观理解 VibeVoice 核心能力的产品种草视频。

整体质感对标专业 Motion Design 工作室的品牌宣传作品。

你拥有完整的创作自由度。

不限制技术路线、动画形式、素材来源或制作工具。

可以使用 Three.js、Remotion、Blender、Canvas、SVG、WebGL、GSAP、FFmpeg、AI 图像与视频生成，以及其他合适的开源项目或工具。

可以混合使用 2D、3D、动态图形、角色动画、动态排版、音频可视化和真实产品演示。

不要求纯代码，也不要求严格复刻分镜图。

分镜图用于传达创意方向，不是限制最终画面的模板。

请根据实际制作效果主动优化构图、运镜、场景、动画和转场。

最终只看成片质量。

二、视频规格

时长：40 秒
画面比例：16:9
分辨率：1920×1080 或更高
帧率：优先 60fps
语言：中文
风格：高级、现代、富有设计感的科技创意动画
音频：有节奏感的背景音乐、必要的音效及真实语音演示
最终格式：MP4

避免廉价霓虹科技风、PPT 式转场、无意义的粒子效果、过度复杂的界面堆砌。

画面要有鲜明的视觉记忆点，不要只靠漂亮的 UI。

三、40 秒完整剧情

第一幕｜声音失控（0–6s）

一段长达 60 分钟的多人录音开始播放。

不同人物的声音混在一起，形成复杂、交错的声音波形。

随着音乐节奏加快，声音逐渐失控，画面充满混乱感。

突然，所有声音停止。

屏幕出现：

「一小时的多人录音，谁说了什么？」

要求：前 3 秒迅速抓住注意力，让观众对接下来的变化产生好奇。

第二幕｜声音有了身份（6–13s）

VibeVoice 登场。

原本混乱的声音开始分离，四位说话人的身份逐渐清晰。

每个人拥有独特的颜色、声音波形和视觉标识。

可以通过人物、抽象角色、动态头像或其他更有创意的方式表现。

四种声音从混乱逐渐变得有序，最终形成清晰的说话人标识。

字幕：

「先分清，谁在说话。」

重点是让观众直观看到说话人识别的能力，而不只是看见四条不同颜色的线。

第三幕｜时间轴魔术（13–23s）

镜头进入声音的内部世界。

一条长达 60 分钟的时间轴逐渐展开。

不同说话人的语音片段被自动标记，并生成对应的文字与时间戳。

每当一个人说话，其对应的声音轨迹和文字同时出现。

镜头可以穿梭于声音、人物、文本和时间轴之间，呈现连续、有节奏的视觉变化。

字幕：

「谁说的，什么时候说的，说了什么。」

「一次整理清楚。」

这一幕是全片的核心高潮，需要最强的视觉表现力。

第四幕｜混乱变成秩序（23–33s）

镜头拉远，刚才复杂的声音世界逐渐整理成一个清晰、有序的语音记录界面。

四位说话人的内容按照时间顺序排列。

观众可以直观看到说话人、时间戳与识别文本的对应关系。

通过动态镜头与交互演示，让观众理解长音频结构化识别的实际价值。

字幕：

「60 分钟长音频，也能结构化识别。」

注意：60 分钟指官方支持的音频长度，不代表能够瞬间完成识别。

第五幕｜结尾反转（33–40s）

所有声音轨道、人物标识和文字逐渐汇聚。

镜头拉远，前面复杂的声音世界最终变成一个简洁的 VibeVoice 标识。

出现：

VibeVoice

Microsoft · Open Source

http://github.com/microsoft/VibeVoice

在观众以为视频结束时，一条小小的声音波形突然再次跳动。

屏幕出现：

「等等，我还有一句！」

伴随一个俏皮的音效，画面结束。

结尾要有趣，不能只是普通的 Logo 动画。

四、视觉与动画要求

你可以重新设计所有场景，但必须保证整支作品拥有统一的美术语言。

重点关注：

视觉创意：尽量用有趣的视觉隐喻表达抽象技术，让声音真正成为画面的主角。
镜头设计：镜头之间具有连贯关系，避免每一幕都是独立的静态画面。
运动质量：动作具有自然的加减速、节奏、重量感和层次。
画面构图：建立清晰的视觉中心，控制留白与信息密度。
动态排版：文字既要清晰易读，也要成为视觉设计的一部分。
音画同步：声音变化、字幕、角色反应和音乐节点准确对应。
情绪变化：从混乱、好奇，到惊喜、清晰，最后用幽默感收尾。

允许为提升成片质量调整镜头时长、动画结构、转场以及视觉表现。

但不要改变核心产品能力，也不要加入未经验证的功能。

五、音乐与声音设计

音乐是这支视频的重要组成部分。

请根据剧情设计一段完整的音乐与音效结构。

开头制造紧张和混乱感；说话人分离时让节奏逐渐清晰；时间轴展开时进入最有冲击力的段落；结尾自然收束并留下一个有趣的声音反转。

可以使用原创电子音乐、Funk、节奏型配乐或其他适合画面的风格。

优先使用真实的 VibeVoice 演示音频。

不强制配音。如果通过音乐、人物声音、字幕和动画能把故事讲清楚，就不要添加多余的解说。

不要为了配音而配音。

六、产品真实性

制作前请阅读 VibeVoice 官方仓库和相关文档，确保产品信息准确。

本片重点展示 VibeVoice-ASR 的：

长音频语音识别
多说话人识别
时间戳生成
结构化文本输出

注意，说话人区分不等同于把混合录音真实分离成多条独立音频文件。

如果无法实际运行 VibeVoice，可以使用官方提供的演示结果进行展示，并明确区分真实输出和概念动画。

不能伪造模型性能、识别准确率或处理速度。

七、制作与质量优化

请自主决定最适合的技术组合和制作流程，不需要拘泥于某一种框架。

可以寻找高质量开源动画库、视觉参考、现成组件或制作工具辅助实现。

但不要为了堆技术而牺牲审美。

制作时遵循以下原则：

先明确全片美术风格、镜头语言和视觉节奏。
按照统一风格完成全部场景。
保证视觉主体、字幕、声音和镜头运动相互配合。
实际渲染并检查关键画面与视频片段。
对人物一致性、动作僵硬、镜头突兀、画面单调、字幕错误和音画不同步等问题主动修正。
如果某种方案实际效果不好，主动更换实现方式，不要坚持错误方向。
优先保证最终作品的整体完成度，而不是单个镜头的炫技效果。

允许反复修改和重新设计，直到形成一支完整、统一、有传播吸引力的作品。

八、最终交付

请完成并提供：

40 秒完整 MP4 视频
可编辑的项目源文件
使用到的素材和音频
必要的渲染或导出说明

如果当前环境不支持某项技术或工具，请自主选择可行的替代方案，不要假装已经完成尚未执行的步骤。

不要只输出制作方案、代码或静态分镜。

最终目标：让观众首先被作品的创意和画面吸引，随后真正理解 VibeVoice 的能力，并产生去 GitHub 了解或尝试这个项目的兴趣。

请直接开始制作，自主完成能够执行的全部工作。

title: Squishy Gummy Bears Playground
author: BorderleSint
prompt:
Build "Gummy Bears" - a single self-contained HTML file (three.js from a CDN is the only dependency): a handful of translucent gummy bears on a white table that you can grab, stretch, squash, throw and pour.

The bears

- Classic gummy bear silhouette: round head with two ears, short snout, plump body, stubby arms and legs, tiny molded eyes and nose
- Every part melts smoothly into the next - build the body as an implicit surface (metaballs / marching cubes), not separate spheres
- Material: real gummy candy. Translucent with transmission and refraction, colored light absorption that gets deeper in thick parts, glossy clearcoat with sharp highlights
- Colors: cherry red, orange, lemon yellow, apple green, clear pineapple
- Soft colored shadow under each bear, tinted by the bear's own color

Physics (this is the whole point - it must feel like jelly, not plastic)

- Each bear is a soft body: mass points for head, ears, snout, body, belly, hands and feet, held together by volume-preserving shape matching
- Limbs and neck are rendered as stretchy strands between points, getting thinner as they stretch
- Grab any part and pull: it stretches like rubber, the rest of the bear leans after it, on release it snaps back with a damped wobble
- Pull the head up: the neck stretches, the body follows, on release the bear squashes and hops
- Press down on the head: the bear pancakes, bulges sideways, then launches itself back up
- Throw a bear: it flies, squashes on landing, bounces and pushes other bears out of the way
- Bears collide with each other and never pass through one another
- Idle bears do small random hops with squash and stretch
- "Pour more bears" drops a handful from above into a wobbling, jiggling pile

UI

- Editorial product-page style on a white background. Large italic serif title "Gummy / Bears.", a short subtitle, a minimal card on the right with flavor swatches, a wobble slider, live "Stretch" and "Bounces" readouts and a "Pour more bears" button
- A subtle circular cursor that grows while grabbing
- ACES tone mapping, environment reflections, soft key and back light. Smooth 60fps

title: Noir Floating Island City Diorama
author: maxt3chno
prompt:
Build "Antropic City": a noir style floating island diorama in three.js with a LEGO minifigure superhero who walks around a plaza in front of the main tower. Use plain ES modules and three.js 0.169.0 through an importmap from jsDelivr. No bundler, no npm. 1 unit = 1 meter. The style is a stylized game asset, not photoreal: simple primitives, clean silhouettes, soft bevels, emissive windows with bloom, soft shadows. Target 60 FPS on an ordinary laptop. Batch static geometry and use InstancedMesh for anything repeated (lamps, trees, windows, raindrops). Never allocate objects per frame. The reference images are the standard. If a number in this prompt disagrees with a reference, match the reference.

STAGE 1. THE CITY
A floating island with a rounded square top (superellipse), shown corner on (rotated 45 degrees). Around the edge: a thick light concrete parapet, square console pylons every 8 m, and a thin wrought iron railing. Underneath: an inverted low poly "diamond" cone with large flat shaded facets and rock strata running dark graphite, then a wide warm brown band, then dark grey, then near black at the tip. Black pipes with elbow bends and glowing amber portholes along the rim. The island slowly hovers and sways.
Around the perimeter: a ring road with dashed markings, curbs and sidewalks. Inside: a grid of streets and cobblestone crossings. Instanced lamp posts, with only 6 to 10 real PointLights near the plaza. A few blocky 1940s cars drive the ring road.
About 25 to 30 stepped art deco buildings in dark graphite and brown stone, with procedural window grids where about 70% of the windows glow warm amber. The centerpiece is Antropic Tower, a stepped ziggurat skyscraper with glowing pilasters, a spire firing a pulsing red orange light beam into the sky, a grand entrance with stairs, and a flickering neon sign reading "ANTROPIC CITY". Around it: a neoclassical courthouse with a golden statue, a clock tower with two glowing dials, a navy blue dome with a gold finial, a water tower on lattice legs, a copper pyramid roof tower, dark conical roof towers with gold spires, low brick tenements with chimneys, an arched viaduct with a red three car train, and conical trees in square planters.
In front of the tower entrance: a perfectly flat walkable plaza, about 34 by 26 m. Art deco sunburst paving, a central statue or fountain, benches, 8 lamps casting warm pools of light, planter trees, and colliders on everything.
Lighting: a cold moonlight directional light with shadows, a hemisphere light and a cold rim light. Warm light comes mostly from windows and lamps. ACES tone mapping, GTAO, UnrealBloom. Keep emissive and bloom restrained so the city never turns into a glowing blur.
Camera: OrbitControls with a home view that frames the whole island. A narrow fov (about 28) and a low elevation (about 11 degrees) keep the rock underside visible below the front corner.

title: Mascot Jump Through 12 Animation Principles
author: 0xSatoshiv
prompt:
00 First try: make Clawd jump onto the other box
01 Arcs: move him along a curve, never a straight line
02 Slow in & out: let him hang at the top, ease in and out of it
03 Squash & stretch: stretch on take-off, squash on landing, same volume
04 Anticipation: crouch down first, so we see the jump coming
05 Follow-through: arms and legs drag behind and settle after he lands
06 Timing: hold the crouch a beat, then snap off fast
07 Solid drawing: lean him into the arc so he has weight
08 Secondary action: eyes on the landing spot, arms flap for balance
09 Pose to pose: key 5 poses: crouch, launch, apex, contact, settle
10 Staging: low 3/4 camera, light on him, dim the rest
11 Exaggeration: jump twice as high and throw in a flip
12 Appeal: stick the landing, then a little ta-da

title: Rewindable Particle Explosion Timeline
author: bonsaixbt
prompt:
I always wondered why AI videos fall apart the moment you try to change anything, so I asked Opus 5.5 to build one where time itself is just a slider I can grab

> one click and the whole interface explodes into thousands of glowing particles
> drag the timeline back and every single one flies home to the exact pixel it came from
> scrub it forward, backward, jerk it around as fast as you want, and it never drifts or glitches
> no After Effects and no hand-placed keyframes, the entire thing is React code rendered with Remotion

The trick is surprisingly simple: nothing in the video remembers what happened before, every frame is calculated from the current time alone, so playing it backwards is exactly as precise as playing it forward

title: 3D Product Trailer From App Screens
author: e1genqq
prompt:
Turn product screens into 3D shots with camera moves, depth of field and controlled lighting.

01 / Install the skills:

▸ http://github.com/remotion-dev/skills
▸ http://github.com/CloudAI-X/threejs-skills

02 / Split the interface into layers

Export UI panels as separate PNGs. Map them onto planes, preserve their proportions and spread them along the Z axis.

Use MeshBasicMaterial so lights don’t change screen brightness. Keep the original components for text updates.

03 / Build repeatable camera moves
Connect the scene through @remotion/three.

Store camera positions, look-at targets and shot timings as data. Drive them with useCurrentFrame() so scrubbing and rendering produce the same movement.

Animate the target too. Otherwise your camera flies past the feature it should demonstrate.

▸ http://remotion.dev/docs/three-canvas

04 / Give it a lens

Use this WebGL effects chain:

RenderPass → BokehPass → UnrealBloomPass → OutputPass

Focus on the active feature. Keep ordinary text below the bloom threshold.

Easy on the glow. It’s a product demo, not a nuclear reactor.

05 / Check cheap. Export clean.

Register the composition as Trailer. Render a smaller draft first:

npx remotion render Trailer out/draft.mp4 --scale=0.5

Check cuts, readable labels and sound. Then export:

npx remotion render Trailer out/final.mp4 --codec=h264 --crf=18

title: LEGO Logo Brick Story Animation
author: lemomo_ai
prompt:
把乐高方标拆成 6 块 2×4 积木，用拼装说明书的版式来演，步骤号一路往上涨。乐高 1932 年在丹麦靠做木头玩具起家，一只能拉着走的木鸭子是早年的招牌，所以第一个拼出来的就是鸭子。为什么是 6 块？乐高官方算过：6 块同色的 2×4 积木，一共有 915,103,765 种拼法。LEGO 这个名字来自丹麦语 leg godt，意思是“好好玩”。6 块积木就有九亿多种玩法，这是对“好好玩”最直接的证明。

方标先拆开，变成 6 块红色的 2×4 积木
积木依次拼成鸭子、塔、楼梯、桥，每一块都按凸点咬合，和我们小时候拼乐高一模一样
画面一角的步骤号一路往上跳，最后停在 915,103,765
积木全部归位，拼回方标，凸点上压着 LEGO

最后那块方标不是终点，只是九亿多种可能里的其中一种。下一秒，它随时可以拆开重新拼。

title: Salt Flat Mirror Cyclist
author: itsfazley
prompt:
Build a cinematic 3D recreation of Bolivia’s Salar de Uyuni mirror effect using Vite, Three.js, and plain JavaScript.

Environment: Create an enormous, perfectly flat salt desert covered by a thin layer of still water. Reproduce the iconic infinite-mirror effect with a vivid blue sky, beautiful white volumetric clouds, and a distant mountain horizon. The sky and its reflection must blend seamlessly across the horizon.

Procedural human cyclist: Generate a convincing human figure entirely from procedural geometry no external models or assets. Use natural human proportions, a smooth head, torso, shoulders, articulated upper arms and forearms, thighs, shins, and feet. Position the rider naturally on the bicycle, with hands gripping the handlebars and feet attached to the pedals. Avoid a blocky or toy-like appearance.

Bicycle: Construct a detailed bicycle with a realistic frame, fork, handlebars, saddle, two wheels with rims and spokes, pedals, crank, chain, and tires. Ensure the cyclist’s proportions and riding position align correctly with the bicycle.

Animation: Animate the bicycle moving slowly across the salt flat. Rotate the wheels and crank, synchronize the rider’s leg movements with the pedals, and add subtle body movement. Keep the hands attached to the handlebars and the feet aligned with the pedals throughout the animation.

Water and reflections: Create a highly reflective, shallow water surface with convincing reflections of the sky, clouds, cyclist, and bicycle. The cyclist’s reflection must remain correctly positioned directly beneath the rider and update continuously as the bicycle moves. Add subtle ripples around the tires without destroying the mirror effect.

Lighting and atmosphere: Use realistic daylight, physically based materials, soft shadows, atmospheric perspective, and natural color grading. Create a seamless transition between the distant horizon, sky, and water reflection.

Camera and composition: Use a cinematic vertical composition inspired by photographs of cyclists crossing Salar de Uyuni. Keep the cyclist relatively small against the vast landscape, with the horizon near the middle of the frame and expansive sky and reflections dominating the scene. Use a slow tracking camera that follows the cyclist smoothly. Support optional mouse orbit and zoom.

Interaction: Add a minimal control panel for pausing the animation, adjusting the cyclist’s speed, switching between camera modes, and toggling daylight intensity.

Technical requirements: Generate everything programmatically using Three.js. No external 3D models, textures, images, videos, or other assets. Organize the code into reusable components, optimize rendering performance, maintain smooth animation, and ensure the scene works responsively on desktop and mobile.

Priority: Photorealistic mirror reflections, natural human anatomy and cycling motion, convincing bicycle geometry, seamless sky-to-water continuity, and cinematic composition. The final result should resemble a real photograph of a lone cyclist crossing an infinite reflective salt desert not a basic 3D demo.

title: Who Pays for the Wires
author: Gdgtify
prompt: Create a 25.00-second kinetic typography film titled **“WHO PAYS FOR THE WIRES?”**  Make it for someone opening an electric bill at their kitchen table. They should finish the film able to explain why a data center can cost money before it uses electricity, and who bears one specific construction risk in AEP Ohio’s service territory.  Deliver one self-contained HTML file with original stereo sound, embedded artwork and type, a 1920 × 1080 capture area, and deterministic 60fps rendering. Give the film the craft of an opening title sequence and the factual precision of a reported graphic.  **The shot to build first**  An eraser sweeps across an architectural drawing. In twelve frames it can remove a building big enough to fill the screen. At the edge of the site, the eraser collides with a steel transmission tower that has already been erected. The pencil shaft flexes. The graphite tip breaks against the paper as the pencil falls. The steel gives one low, sustained note.  Hold on the empty site and the standing tower. Let the viewer discover the question a beat before the words arrive.  Everything before this shot prepares the distinction between *planned* and *built*. Everything after it follows the cost of what remains.  **One world, three materials**  Build a single tabletop set. An opened utility envelope, a household bill, a translucent engineering drawing, and a contract occupy different depths. Behind the table, one warm kitchen window establishes a human scale. Keep the household bill anonymous and its dollar amount outside the crop.  Use graphite for proposed work. A soft mark can be drawn, smeared, or erased. Use dull galvanized steel for installed infrastructure. It casts a hard shadow and has real mass. Use dark red ink for financial obligations. It moves through the contract and invoice while the steel stays planted on the site.  Set the headlines in a heavy, slightly narrow grotesque. Set the contract paraphrase in a readable book serif. The type should look like it belongs to the surface carrying it. During a fast move, one word can become architecture. During its reading hold, give the viewer its complete silhouette.  **0.00–3.00 seconds · The envelope**  Start in near darkness. Paper slides across wood. A kitchen light catches the embossed words **ELECTRIC BILL**. One thumb holds the envelope against the table while a finger opens the fold. Give the paper a little resistance. The sound is close enough to hear the fibers separate.  From this low angle, the fold makes a roofline. Move along it until a printed rule on the bill meets a survey line on the translucent plan underneath. Follow that line into the plan. In the margin, establish **ILLUSTRATIVE PROJECT**. The site and cancellation are a hypothetical example.  **3.00–7.50 seconds · Build two different futures**  Reveal **PROPOSED DATA CENTER** in graphite. The crossbars of the letters extend into a floor plan. Rack aisles draw themselves in quick succession. Leave a small square gap at the far end of the building. The viewer will recognize that patch of bare paper after the erasure.  In the foreground, the phrase **GRID WORK BEGINS** lands. Use the strokes of GRID as fabrication guides. Steel members lift off the guides, rotate around visible joints, and bolt into a single tower. Give the tower one distinctive asymmetrical gusset plate. A cable settles into its insulator with a short downward sag.  Keep both states readable in one low tracking shot. Behind the tower, a building still made of pencil. In front, steel already casting a shadow. The score borrows its rhythm from the work. Two bolt strikes, a cable pluck, a pencil stroke. Build the bass underneath those sounds.  **7.50–11.50 seconds · Cancel the project**  Across the top edge of the drawing, typeset **WHAT IF THE DEVELOPER CANCELS?** Let CANCELS travel with the eraser while the rest of the question holds steady.  Execute the pencil shot. Give the disappearing rack lines a dry directional smear. Let the last graphite dust settle around the tower footing. The kitchen light keeps shining through the same window. The audience should feel the peculiar ordinariness of a project that simply stops.  Land **BEFORE POWER IS SWITCHED ON** beside the empty site. A small service switch, previously visible on the plan margin, stays open. Omit the server-fan crescendo the score has led us to expect. Leave the steel ringing.  **11.50–15.00 seconds · Find the cost**  Lock the camera for half a second. Across the vacant footprint, place **THE WIRES ARE ALREADY UP.**  Then lower the camera until the tower’s diagonal brace fills the frame. Follow its shadow across the paper. The shadow meets a red invoice rule at precisely the same angle. Move from one to the other in a continuous shot. The solid tower remains visible behind us in the reflection of a metal ruler.  Reveal **WHO PAYS?** Set WHO small enough to fit between the strokes of the monumental P in PAYS. Let the question mark land over the original envelope. Hold the empty space beneath it. This is where a viewer might expect to see their own name.  **15.00–20.50 seconds · Read the agreement**  Slide the translucent drawing aside. Beneath it is the contract that has been on the table since the opening. A red rule leads to the source label **AEP OHIO · DATA CENTER AGREEMENT**. Present the operative condition in editorial type, clearly identified as a paraphrase.  Use three successive reading holds.  **CUSTOMER CANCELS BEFORE POWER-UP**  **DATA CENTER CUSTOMER REIMBURSES THE UTILITY**  **100% OF BUILDOUT COSTS**  Keep the condition and the AEP Ohio label visible when **100%** lands. Give **OF BUILDOUT COSTS** enough room to read at the same glance as the number. That wording defines exactly what the percentage covers.  Build the percentage sign from objects already on the table. Two punched registration holes supply the circles. The camera slides until the tower brace aligns between them to form the slash. The viewpoint clicks into place and **100%** reads as a single piece of typography. Hold it for at least 1.4 seconds. A viewer who pauses here should get a complete, accurately qualified frame.  Sound the answer with the same three notes heard during construction, now tapped on the desk with a pencil. Let the final note coincide with the registration of the percent sign.  **20.50–25.00 seconds · Return to the kitchen**  Pull back. The household bill occupies the near side of the table. Across from it, the project invoice sits on the developer’s agreement. The red obligation line ends there. Between the two documents stands the same tower, its gusset plate catching the kitchen light.  The final copy belongs in the empty building footprint.  **WHO PAYS FOR THE WIRES?**   **IN THIS OHIO CASE, THE DATA CENTER CUSTOMER.**  Hold this composition from approximately 21.7 to 24.2 seconds. Finish with the sound of the pencil stub rolling across the table and coming to rest against the tower footing. The kitchen light goes out. Reach black by 24.85 seconds.  **Sound and pacing**  Write the score at 144 BPM, giving 15 bars in 25 seconds. Let construction sounds push against the beat. Place the pencil break between beats so it feels like an interruption. Reserve the strongest bass resonance for the standing tower after the project disappears. A quieter, closer kitchen sound at the end should make the return to the household tangible.  Generate the full score and effects as one original 48 kHz stereo buffer, exactly 1,200,000 samples per channel. Drive playback from the audio clock. Use the same cue records for the bolt landings, eraser contact, pencil break, percentage alignment, and their sounds.  **Reporting and delivery**  Use the cancellation provision in AEP Ohio’s Letter of Agreement as the factual basis. Its trigger in this example is customer cancellation before the target energization date. Keep the **100%** attached to the covered buildout costs. Keep household bills unquantified. Put the full source, the 2025 approval date, the November 2026 reporting context, and the separate provision for a delay exceeding 12 months in a source panel outside the film.  Provide **Play with sound**, pause, replay, scrub, and WAV download outside capture. Expose `window.ready`, `window. seek(seconds)`, `window.renderFrame(n)`, and `window.cues`. Render frames 0–1499 at `n/60`. Make dust, cable sag, lighting, camera position, and type placement reconstructible from any timestamp.  Review the erasure through the contract reveal first **with the sound off**. The material change alone should tell the story. Then play it with sound and check that the pencil break gets room to register before WHO PAYS enters. At half resolution, verify that the cancellation condition, responsible customer, and scope of the 100% figure can all be read. Check the opening and closing frames for the black loop boundary. Report which checks were actually executed.

title: Pachinko-Style Chatbot vs Agent Explainer
author: tankazunori0914
prompt:
会話型AI と AIエージェント の違いを、パチンコの激アツリーチ演出で魅せるアニメーションGIFにしてください。内容は薄くてOK、ただし嘘はNG。インパクト最優先、でも文字は読める速さで。

【お題】
「来週、Aさんと30分の会議を入れて」という依頼で対決させる。
会話型AIは調整メールの文面までは完璧に書けるが、送信やカレンダー登録はできない。
AIエージェントはツールを使って、予定確認 → 空き照合 → 承認 → 招待送信まで進めて完了させる。

【演出の流れ】
1. 「ドパ注意」警告（黄黒ストライプ＋赤点滅）→ 左右から迫ってVS着弾
2. ROUND 1：会話型AI
 チャット画面に調整メールがタイピング表示 → 「文面HIT!!」
 → 「送信とカレンダー登録はご自身でお願いします」で縦線ガーン
 → 弱点テロップ「考えて書けるけど、手は動かせない」
3. 保留が青→緑→赤→金に変化 → 擬似連NEXT×3 → リーチ!! → 虹背景で激アツ
 → 役物落下でAIエージェント降臨（カレンダー・メール・検索のツールアイコンが装着される）
4. ROUND 2：AIエージェント
 光の玉がツールをたどってHOPする
 HOP 1：カレンダーで自分の予定を確認
 HOP 2：Aさんの空き枠と照合して候補を決定
 HOP 3：「この内容で送信しますか？」→ 画面中央に「PUSH!!」ボタン演出 → 人が承認
 → 招待送信 →「予定登録 確定!!」で紙吹雪
5. 比較表（できること／動き方／リスク／向いている仕事）
 → AIエージェントにWINスタンプ。ただし「手軽さと安全性は会話型AIに軍配」「相談や壁打ちなら会話型で十分」も入れる
 → 結論「考えるなら会話型、動かすならエージェント。使い分けた人が、勝ち。」

【仕様】

・640×360、12fps、20〜30秒、無限ループ、15MB以内

・音の代わりに画面揺れ・白フラッシュ・集中線・後光で盛る
・テロップは最低1秒止める
・実在のサービス名やロゴは使わず、汎用アイコンで描く

title: Shake the Jelly Candy Jar
author: bluumik
prompt:
Build a single-file interactive 3D web experience called "Jelly Sweets." using Three.js (WebGL), all procedural, zero external assets. A jar of soft pastel jelly candies is shaken onto a round plate, and the candies bounce, wobble and settle with satisfying squishy physics.

LOOK AND FEEL
- Deep plum to near-black background with a soft violet vignette glow behind the plate that shifts slightly with the chosen flavor.
- Serif title "Jelly Sweets." top left with a small italic subtitle "The Sweet Shop Collection".
- A round, shallow, frosted glass plate with a glossy white rim, seen from a three-quarter top view, with a soft shadow beneath.
- Small refined UI. Quiet luxury, like a limited edition candy shop display.

THE CANDIES
- A mix of soft shapes: round gumdrops, striped pill-like candies, rounded cube marshmallow-style pieces, and small beads.
- Translucent jelly material with soft glossy highlights, gentle subsurface glow and fine surface bumps. Striped candies have soft diagonal stripes.
- Pastel flavors: strawberry pink, lemon yellow, lime green, sky blue, grape purple, peach. A set mostly shares the chosen flavor with small tone variation.
- 6 to 12 candies by default, with a stepper to change the amount.

JELLY PHYSICS
- Rigid body motion plus a soft-body wobble layer: candies squash on impact, bulge, jiggle and recover with damping.
- Candies collide with each other and the plate rim with believable friction, then settle gently, sometimes balancing on each other.
- Candies that fall off the plate respawn above it or are caught by an invisible rim.
- Click and drag a candy to pick it up and toss it, with a soft follow-through.

CONTROLS
- A large pink pill button "Shake the jar" that launches all candies upward with a random but pleasant impulse (also Space bar).
- Candy count stepper (1 to 20) with minus and plus buttons.
- Flavor swatches along the bottom left. Switching one smoothly tints all candies and the ambient glow.
- Top right buttons: "Room view" and "Table view" (a wider camera and a closer camera) plus "Settings".
- Settings panel: jelly stiffness slider, auto-rotate toggle, sound on or off.
- Keyboard: Space to shake, plus and minus for the count, T to switch views.

SOUND AND POLISH
- Soft squishy plops and light clicks synthesized with WebAudio (no files), pitch and volume tied to impact speed.
- 60 fps, adaptive pixel ratio, filmic tone mapping, gentle bloom on highlights, soft contact shadows on the plate.
- Smooth camera orbit with inertia and an optional gentle auto-rotate.
- Works on desktop and mobile touch. Clean, commented code in one HTML file with constants grouped at the top.
