title: Paper Plane Anime Short Film
author: anstapnever
prompt:
Create a 2D anime short. It must look completely like real Japanese anime, as if it were taken directly from a finished theatrical anime film. This is traditional-looking, hand-drawn 2D anime, not a 3D animation, a moving illustration, or a stylized web graphic.

Build everything with code: plan every move as keyed tracks in JS and bake them per frame, build the world in Blender from Python and render it in Eevee, then paint each frame in a second pass with numpy and OpenCV, and encode with ffmpeg. Deliver one 1920x1080, 24 fps MP4, 71.5 seconds, 15 shots, no voice and no text. Animate characters on twos and effects on threes; the camera and the plane move on every frame. Use any tools, libraries, references, guides, literally anything, as long as the final result looks 100% like hand-drawn 2D anime.

WORLD
A summer meadow at sunset, real scale in centimetres: grass taller than the hero, a pebble, flowers, stalks, a dragonfly, a dew web, a mound with a steep edge over a lower meadow. Painted cloud towers with golden rims. The sun sets from 9 to 0.5 degrees and the hill shadow climbs.

CHARACTERS
The hero is the Claude mascot: a tiny terracotta cube (#D97757) about 1.9 cm tall, with a big readable face. The prop is a paper plane folded from a notebook corner, 4.2 cm long, grid paper, a crayon sun drawn on the right wing. A dragonfly flies with them.

STORY
The hero stands on a pebble, arms out, jumps for a seed, flaps and flops face first into the grass. The plane crashes beside it in a burst of pollen. It climbs into the fold and a gust lifts them over the meadow. It steers round stalks, waves at a dragonfly and does not see the dew web. The wet wing droops and they spiral into the shadow of the hill. The hero tows the plane up the hill by a web thread, racing the band of light, dries the wing in the last sun and runs it off the cliff edge. The plane drops out of frame. Silence. Then the evening updraft lifts it into the sunset. The hero stands on the nose, arms out, and sneezes from the pollen.

LIGHT
The sun is in frame and behind the hero most of the time: backlight, rays through the grass, a warm rim, bloom, lens flare and bokeh. Gouache brushwork on the background, ink lines on the hero, paper texture and fine grain over everything. Light only changes with a cause you can see: the hill shadow, the sunset.

SOUND
A fully synthesized score, no samples and no voice, built on one flight theme in D major: a hopeful plucked motif when it tries to fly, a comic flop, the whoosh and the pollen burst, the theme on strings, glass and electric piano in flight, the dragonfly's buzz, a glassy shimmer and splash at the web, a minor fall in the spiral, a dark pad in the shade, a stubborn ostinato up the hill, silence at the empty edge, and the theme in full as it rises into the sunset. A sneeze and a laugh at the end.

CHECKS
Before the final render a script tests every frame: the hero, the plane and the camera never go through the ground, a stalk, the pebble or each other. Zero hits before rendering.

title: Container Ships in a Storm at Sea
author: itsfazley
prompt:
Build "Storm at Sea" a fully procedural Three.js (r160, ES modules via importmap from jsDelivr) scene, no external models/textures/audio. Modular files: waves, ocean, sky, ship, motion, weather, audio, textures, main.

OCEAN: 12-wave Gerstner sum (wavelengths 9–235 m, Hs ≈14 m, deep-water dispersion), identical math in GLSL and JS. Camera-centred polar grid (~560 rings × 512 segs, denser near camera), per-pixel normals + Jacobian, fade small waves by distance. Shading: deep teal body, crest subsurface scatter, Fresnel sky reflection, whitecaps from Jacobian + crest height using Worley-cell foam, wind-row streaks, hull/bow foam + Kelvin wake per ship, exp² fog matched to sky. Add a travelling rogue-wave packet (Gaussian envelope, ~11 m) every ~90 s.

SKY: shader dome, 3-layer fbm storm deck, horizon light gap, rain curtains, lightning lights the clouds. PMREM env from the sky for wet metal.

SHIP (procedural, highly detailed, ~230 m post-Panamax): lofted hull (bow flare, raked stem, bulbous bow, transom overhang, skeg), canvas-painted hull (antifouling, boot top, plate seams + bump, rust streaks, draft marks, Plimsoll, thruster symbols, name/brand lettering), forecastle with windlasses, chains, anchors, bollards, foremast; breakwater; hatch covers; ~1,500 instanced 20/40 ft containers (corrugated/door textures, weighted colors, AO by tier, varied stack heights); lashing bridges + rods; accommodation tower with lit windows, stairs, lifeboats on davits; enclosed bridge + wings; mast with rotating radars, radomes, antennas; raked elliptical funnel with company band + smoke; rudder + spinning 5-blade propeller; nav lights as additive sprites. Merge static parts per material. Three ships, different liveries.

MOTION: heave/pitch/roll as damped oscillators driven by hull-sampled wave heights; bow-slam detection → spray bursts + green water; prop racing when stern lifts.

title: Night Shift Warehouse Cartoon
author: polinaaAi
prompt:
Introducing Night Shift: a 25 second 3D cartoon where Claude gets buried in 4,812 orders, then automates the whole shift

1 HTML file + 0 keyframes + 6 minutes of render = 25 seconds at 60 fps

The story in 4 beats:

→ 2:00 AM, the belt speeds up and the board climbs from 120 to 480 units an hour

→ a box lands on Clawd's head, the belt jams, the pile buries everything but the eyes

→ Clawd bursts out, types claude into a terminal, two robot arms wake up and sort every box into its zone on the beat

→ 6:00 AM, dawn through the skylight, Clawd in a hammock with coffee, the board reads SHIFT DONE

Here's how it's built:

step 1 → Claude Opus 5.5 writes the whole scene in Three.js inside Claude Code, one renderAt(t) function draws any frame from the time alone

step 2 → the belt speed is integrated every 10 ms, so each box sits exactly where the speed curve puts it, even when the belt goes 8x faster

step 3 → the robot arms use 2-joint inverse kinematics to reach each box, grip it and drop it in the right bin

step 4 → the quota board, the terminal and the clock are live canvas textures redrawn every frame

step 5 → the soundtrack is synthesized: a hum, a scanner beep for every passing box, a siren on the jam, a servo whir on every pick

step 6 → headless Chrome renders 3,000 frames at 120 fps, ffmpeg blends them to 60 fps with motion blur

title: Fear Itself Recursive Typography Film

Roosevelt names fear as the thing that traps you: self-referential, nameless, paralyzing, a retreat that feeds itself. Visualize this literally with an infinite recursive composition (the Droste effect). - For most of the film the camera falls endlessly inward through a typographic Art Deco frame that contains itself. - On "convert retreat into advance," the direction of infinity reverses. The fall inward becomes a climb outward, and the camera breaks out of the recursion into open space for the first time.  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 1. Make no network requests. Silent autoplay preview, play/pause, and a scrubber, all outside the captured frame. Return a working implementation.  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 2. Capitalization may change. No added words.  Final attribution (not spoken): FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT FIRST INAUGURAL ADDRESS · WASHINGTON · 4 MARCH 1933  The timing is authored. Do not claim synchronization with the 1933 recording.  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 3. THE CORE TECHNIQUE: EXPLICIT RECURSION, NOT FEEDBACK ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Define one "panel": an Art Deco composition with an inner window. The inner window holds an exact copy of the panel scaled by k = 0.28, positioned at an authored anchor that is not the panel's center, so the zoom path spirals. Every frame, draw the panel recursively at depth levels 0 to 7, from the deepest level outward, using the composite transform T^n.  The infinite zoom: - Camera zoom z(t) = k^(−φ(t)), with the fractional part of φ cycling. - Because the image at level n+1 equals the image at level n scaled by k, the loop is seamless. - The camera transform's fixed point is the recursion's fixed point. Compute it analytically from the anchor and k.  Panel content changes over time. Each recursion level shows the panel's content at a time offset of n × Δ (Δ = 0.35 s). The deeper layers are therefore earlier in the sentence, and words visibly "fall away" into the past as the camera passes through them. Do not use any frame-feedback buffer. The recursion is redrawn from vector data every frame, so seeking is exact.  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 4. VISUAL IDENTITY: 1933 ART DECO, RADIO AGE ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Palette: - Gunmetal # 14171A - Nickel # BFC3C2 - Brass # B48A4A - Cream # EFE7D3 - One accent: signal red # B3352A, used only for FEAR and TERROR  The panel frame is a stepped Art Deco proscenium of nested chevrons and sunburst rays, drawn as thin double rules in brass and nickel. It looks machined and metallic, using linear gradients.  Typography (embed OFL faces): - Poiret One (thin geometric deco) for connective words - a high-contrast Didone (Bodoni Moda Black) for the stress words - a monoline geometric sans (Josefin Sans Bold, wide tracking) for labels inside the frame  Texture: subtle stationary brushed-metal noise attached to panel coordinates, so it scales with each recursion level. Never apply screen-space grain.  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 5. STORYBOARD ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 0.00–0.40 Black.  0.40–3.40 "So, first of all, let me assert my firm belief" A single panel faces the viewer, stable, with no zoom yet. The camera falls toward the inner window. "the only thing we have to" occupies the frame's lintel. FEAR (in red) sits inside the inner window, so the camera is falling toward fear.  6.20–8.60 "is fear itself—" THE RECURSION REVEALS ITSELF. - Inside the window, the panel repeats with FEAR inside it, again and again. - At "itself," the camera's fall reaches cruising speed: one full recursion level every 0.9 s. - Every level's FEAR is the same word, receding: fear made of fear. - The em dash is drawn as a long brass rule that the camera passes through.  8.60–12.40 "nameless, unreasoning, unjustified" Three typographic decays, one per word, applied to the text inside the current outermost level: - NAMELESS: the letters of every visible word lose their identity. Their glyph outlines morph (by interpolating points along normalized contours) into blank Deco nameplates: empty rounded rectangles of the same width. - UNREASONING: the panel's ruled structure bends. Straight rules warp along a smooth sine displacement, and the chevrons lose their symmetry. - UNJUSTIFIED (the typographic pun): the word appears inside a fully justified four-line text block made of the sentence so far. On landing, the block literally un-justifies: the word spacing collapses, the right edge goes ragged, and the lines fall out of alignment. The block must visibly start justified.  12.40–15.60 "terror which paralyzes" TERROR (in red) fills the inner window at the next level. On PARALYZES, the zoom stops dead within 3 frames: the infinite fall freezes. Everything locks: - the sunburst rays stop - the deeper levels stop Hold 30 frames of absolute stillness, the paralysis. Only the word PARALYZES is visible as new, with a hairline brass frame snapping around it.  15.60–18.60 "needed efforts to convert" Effort: the panel's chevron frame acts as gears. The stepped Deco borders rotate in opposing directions, in small detented ticks of 6° each, held for 4 frames, like a mechanism being cranked. - NEEDED EFFORTS sits on the lintel. - CONVERT is set as a word that rotates 180° about its horizontal axis on landing. Draw the flip as a real foreshortening of the outline (scaleY through zero) with a nickel-to-brass shading change at the back face.  18.60–21.80 "retreat into advance." THE REVERSAL. - RETREAT appears inside the window. The camera's zoom direction reverses: φ(t) decreases, so the camera rises outward through the levels, and the deeper copies now rush toward the viewer. - As the camera exits level 0, the outermost panel frame opens: its two halves part like elevator doors, the first time any panel has been incomplete. - The camera emerges into open space for the first time in the film. There is a wide horizon of fine brass sunburst rays. - ADVANCE stands alone in Bodoni Black, cream, full width.  21.80–23.80 Final composition Hold on ADVANCE. The recursion is visible behind it as a small, receding framed object, now finite and behind us. The attribution appears at the lower edge.  23.80–25.00 Closure The sunburst rays retract to the vanishing point in sequence. Black by 24.90. Frame 25.00 must equal frame 0.00.  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 6. title: Seminar Announcement Video Director
author: Bob_zaimu
prompt:
あなたは告知動画のディレクターです。HyperFrames（npx hyperframes）で、30秒・1920×1080・ナレーションなしの告知動画を、私と会話しながら作ってください。

■進め方
1. まず私に1つずつ質問して内容を集める（何の告知か／伝えたい一言／タイトル／日時（年も）／参加方法と申込み先／登壇者／特典／ロゴ（透過PNG推奨）／伏せたいこと）。分からないことは作らずに聞く。
2. そろったら10場面前後の絵コンテ（storyboard.html）を作ってファイルリンクで見せ、OpenTracks（http://opentracks.com）から「かっこいい・盛り上がる」BGM候補を3曲、試聴リンク付きで出す。私がOKするまで制作しない。
3. OK後に制作。BGMの一番盛り上がる頭を「問い」の場面に合わせ、切り替えを拍にそろえる。BGMは背景でうっすら。lint・checkを通し、コマ一覧を自分の目で確かめてから書き出す。
4. 完成MP4と、完成画面入りの絵コンテをリンクで渡す。BGMの山が合っているか、耳での確認を私に頼む。

■デザイン（毎回これで）
・濃紺 #0B1024 の背景に、紙色 #F2EFE8 の場面を2つ挟む
・ゴールド #FFC940＝望ましい側・日付／マゼンタ #E0367F＝否定／シアン #5CE1E6＝全編を通る1本の線（仕切り→下線→打ち消し線→最後の枠）
・見出し Noto Sans JP 900（使う文字だけ埋め込む）、数字 Archivo Black、ラベル JetBrains Mono、英字の差し色 Instrument Serif Italic
・四隅にトンボ・場面番号・タイムコード・日時、下端に進行バー
・演出：1語ずつ組み上げて大きくドン／左右の対比とvs／デザインツール風の選択枠／集中線で問い／打ち消し線／数字のカウント（中身は「？」で伏せる）／マーカー線／タイトルは長めに静止／斜めの帯と紙吹雪／最後に日付ドン
・流れ：断言→対立→問い→通説の否定→答えの予告（伏せる）→タイトル→登壇者と参加方法→特典→日付

■約束
答えは言いすぎず、当日への期待で終える。写真・ロゴは私が渡したものだけ使う。BGM・効果音のダウンロードは私が選んでから。投稿は私がする。

prompt:

title: Voxel Ringed Capital City Flythrough
author: VulKan42069
prompt:
Create a single self-contained HTML file using Three.js loaded from a CDN, with all code inline and no other external assets, that plays a breathtaking 60-second cinematic flythrough of a vast, original, full-scale medieval capital city, built entirely in a charming, detailed voxel art style from small flat-coloured cubes, with warm golden-hour lighting, soft shadows, gentle ambient occlusion, drifting cube clouds, strong atmospheric haze so distant districts fade softly into the light and the city feels truly enormous, a soft bloom on the sun, letterbox bars and filmic tone mapping.

LAYOUT: The city is built at true scale, many kilometres across, on a broad green river plain, and is laid out as three perfectly concentric circular rings of colossal walls, like ripples spreading from a single centre point. The walls are immense — far taller than any building, around fifty metres high — sheer, smooth and pale weathered stone, their outer faces ribbed with rows of tall rectangular buttress pillars running from base to top, giving them a rhythmic, monumental look, with a flat walkway along the summit. The vast fields of land between the rings are mostly open green farmland, pasture, forest patches and small villages, so the rings feel enormous and isolated.

WALLED TOWNS: Each ring wall is broken at the four compass points (north, south, east and west) by a walled town district that bulges outward from the ring wall in a deep U shape. Each one is enclosed by the same towering buttressed wall curving around it, and the space inside is packed edge to edge with thousands of tightly crowded houses with brown, terracotta and slate roofs, timber-framed upper floors and smoking chimneys, threaded by narrow winding lanes. At the heart of each town stands a large plaza with a grand stone town hall, and a straight stone-lined canal runs down the middle of the town, passing through a huge arched water gate in the outer curve and another into the ring beyond. A great gate with a drawbridge sits beside the canal at the outer tip. These twelve towns line up exactly along four straight axes from the centre outward, so the whole city reads from above as a perfect target crossed by a giant plus sign. A winding river enters from the north, flows through the canals of the northern towns and the very centre, and leaves through the southern towns, while straight canals and grand avenues link the eastern and western towns through the centre, crossing the river at a great central crossroads square. Watchtowers on the walls fly long red banners, one of which carries @vulkan42069 in bold cube letters. Everything is sized so that houses look like grains beside the walls and a single walled town is a whole city in itself.

INNER CITY: The innermost ring is completely filled with the capital itself: a grand white castle with tall towers and a cathedral beside it on a gentle hill beside the central crossroads, surrounded by stone mansions with courtyards, formal gardens, a clock tower, market squares, an amphitheatre, church spires, and dense neighbourhoods of houses, with wharves, boats and waterwheels along the river and arched stone bridges crossing it.

OUTSIDE THE WALLS: Beyond the outermost ring, a patchwork of farmland, windmills, orchards, scattered villages and dark forests stretches for miles along roads that radiate from the four outer towns, rising toward rolling forested hills and distant snow-capped mountains.

LIFE: Bring the city to life with tiny voxel details: banners fluttering, boats drifting along the river and canals, carts rolling through the gates, flocks of birds wheeling over the rooftops, chimney smoke rising, windmill sails and waterwheels turning, and lanterns flickering on along the wall tops and in windows as the light fades.

PERFORMANCE: To render this scale smoothly, build the houses from a dozen varied templates using instanced meshes, place them procedurally along a generated network of winding lanes with a fixed seed so every town looks dense, organic and never repetitive, build the ring walls, U-shaped town walls and buttress pillars procedurally from instanced cube segments following their curves, merge static geometry by ring and town, and use simpler level-of-detail versions for distant buildings.

TIMELINE (single timeline, smooth, slow, majestic camera moves with gentle cuts):
- 0–10 s: the camera descends through the clouds high above the plain, looking straight down, revealing the whole city at once — three perfect concentric rings, twelve bulging walled towns and the river-and-canal cross — laid out like a giant target below, stretching almost to the horizon.
- 10–20 s: it tilts forward and glides low across the farmland along the southern road, past turning windmills, toward the outer southern town, rising slowly up the sheer buttressed face of its colossal curved wall and sweeping over the top to reveal the town below packed solid with rooftops, its canal and town hall plaza, and the next ring wall looming in the haze beyond.
- 20–32 s: it drops down and follows the canal and river north, through the arched water gates and across the open green land between the rings, then through the middle and inner towns, skimming under stone bridges and past wharves, waterwheels and boats, with houses rising steeply on both banks.
- 32–42 s: it climbs out over the central crossroads and banks in a sweeping arc along the curve of the inner ring wall, over crowded districts and market squares, weaving between the clock tower and church spires toward the castle hill.
- 42–52 s: it slowly orbits the grand castle and cathedral, banners streaming, as the sun lowers and warm lights begin to glow in windows across the whole city and along all three ring walls.
- 52–60 s: it rises and pulls back into a vast, slow, top-down aerial view of the entire ringed city glowing in the sunset, three great circles of wall lanterns forming glowing rings and the twelve towns glittering like jewels on them, the river and canals shimmering in a cross, the countryside fading into dusk, before drifting back up into the clouds to match the opening and loop seamlessly.

SOUND: Add sound generated with the Web Audio API for wind high above the clouds, distant church bells, a lively murmur of city life, river water and creaking waterwheels, birdsong, and a sweeping, majestic orchestral score that swells as the city is revealed and settles gently at the end, starting only after the user clicks a sound toggle.

TECHNICAL: Make the canvas fill the browser window and resize responsively, include small buttons to pause, replay and mute, build everything from voxels with instanced meshes rather than imported models or images, and keep the code clean and smooth-running when the file is opened directly in a modern browser.

title: Jelly Pufferfish Soft-Body Study
author: Bengiyai
prompt:
Build a single-file interactive three.js (r170, ES module via import map) soft-body study called "Puffer Jelly", No. 059 in a "Material Studies" series. A long-spine porcupinefish cast in two layers of jelly rests on its belly on a pale studio table, fins out, lips pursed. Handled gently, it stays calm. Treat it roughly and it gulps water and inflates into a spiky ball, then slowly lets the air out when left alone.
Geometry (signed distance field, two rest poses):
- Calm body: a thick teardrop of smooth-unioned ellipsoids. Big blunt forehead, widest just behind the eyes, a soft belly pressed flat on the table, and a fast taper to a short tail stalk. Fleshy pursed lips at the front, eyes on raised bumps high on the head.
- Puffed body: almost a sphere, about three times the calm volume, with the eyes, the lips (now a round open "O") and the tail stalk still sticking out. Map every calm rest point onto it along rays from the body centre, so both poses share one mesh and one lattice. The belly fills first.
- Fins: a rounded tail fan, small dorsal and anal fins set far back, and two paddle-shaped pectoral fins just behind the eyes. Each is a thin membrane stretched between rays, scalloped between them.
- Spines: about 400 sugar thorns with flared tripod roots, spread evenly over the skin (none on the eyes or lips). Calm, they lie flat toward the tail. Puffed, they stand straight out, about 2.5 times longer, rising in a wave from head to tail.
- Inside: about 20 small trapped air bubbles that drift apart as the body swells.
Simulation:
- Hex lattice with 5 tets per cell, boundary nodes snapped to the surface and a node layer exactly on the floor.
- CPU XPBD shape matching on a fixed 60 Hz step with 10 substeps. The head and fin bases are firmer than the belly.
- Render meshes from surface nets (clear jelly plus a cream core layer), embedded barycentrically in the tets.
- Inflation is a muscle made by rewriting rest shapes: every rest length and shape-matching target blends from the calm pose toward the puffed pose, so the body swells through the physics, overshoots and wobbles. Puffed, the jelly is stiffer and bounces like a ball on its spine tips.
- Fins are stiff at the base and soft at the tip, so they lag behind the body. The pectorals scull all the time and the eyes turn toward the pointer.
Temper:
- A stress value from 0 to 100% that slowly decays. A single click adds a little, each quick click in a row adds more than the last, and dragging fast or shaking adds stress too. Slow drags add nothing and calm it faster.
- Under 35% it only dents, wobbles and flicks its fins. From 35% the spines half lift and shiver. At 70% it gulps 8 times, about half a second apart, and each gulp inflates it one visible step.
- Left alone for 4 seconds while puffed, it exhales over about 4 seconds and folds its spines from tail to head.
Rendering (hand-written ShaderMaterials):
- Key-light shadow map, a back-face thickness pass, and refraction through the front faces with Beer–Lambert absorption and a scattering tint.
- Clear jelly in the fish's natural colours: warm tan #A88553 on the back fading to #C9AE84 on the flanks, soft brown blotches #6E4B27, small white freckles and dark speckles. All marks live in body coordinates, so they stretch apart as it puffs, and each has a subtle bump.
- The cream layer #EFE9DC fills the belly up to a soft line low on the flank, and fills the lips.
- A soft pink mouth that opens into a round "O" as it puffs.
- Eyes are glossy beads: a big black pupil, a flecked gold-brown iris and a dark teal rim.
- Fins are clear yellow jelly #E8C640 with darker rays. Spines are ivory sugar, clearer toward the tip.
- Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping and 4× MSAA.
Camera: one fixed three-quarter view from about 45° above, with the fish in the middle at about a third of the screen width and plenty of empty table around it. No auto-orbit; drag empty space to orbit.
Interaction:
- Click to poke. Drag any part to pull the jelly; lift it and let go to drop it.
- Buttons: Puff, Calm, Reset. Sliders: Firmness, Internal damping, Temper. Checkboxes: ¼ speed, Show mesh. A Pause button.
UI:
- Editorial layout on a warm grey backdrop (#e2dfda): an italic serif title "Puffer Jelly.", the caption "Calm under a gentle hand. Too rough, and it gulps water into a spiky ball.", a specimen panel marked "fig. 59", and a status pill "THREE.JS · LIVE".
- Live readouts: stress and inflation as bars, length and girth in cm (scale 1 unit ≈ 28 cm), mass in g from enclosed volume at 1.05 g/cm³, pokes, and state (Calm, Alarmed, Puffing, Puffed, Exhaling).
- A collapsible "Inside the experiment" notes section.
- Responsive stacked layout on phones, a WebGL2 fallback message, prefers-reduced-motion support. English UI throughout.

title: The Island That Woke Up
author: halfofthemwork
prompt:
Create a single self-contained HTML file using Three.js that renders a beautiful animated voxel-art 3D scene: "The Island That Woke Up". It tells a short wordless story with a huge reveal of scale, in a seamless 20-second cycle.

THE STORY:
0-4s, THE STORM: Close on a tiny wooden fishing boat with a patched red sail and one warm lantern, tossed by towering dark voxel waves at night. Heavy rain, wind-blown foam, black clouds, and lightning that lights up the whole scene. In one lightning flash, a colossal dark shape is briefly visible under the water, right below the boat.
4-9s, THE RISE: The sea around the boat starts to bulge. The boat is lifted on a growing hill of water, then the water drains away in dozens of voxel waterfalls. A cozy island emerges beneath it: a striped lighthouse, a small harbor, crooked fishing houses with glowing windows, palm trees, moss, coral and barnacles. The boat comes to rest safely in the harbor, and the lighthouse beam switches on.
9-13s, THE REVEAL: The camera keeps pulling back, and the island turns out to be the shell of a gigantic sea turtle. Its huge ancient head rises from the sea with water pouring off it, and one amber eye slowly opens. Four enormous flippers start to beat, and the turtle lifts out of the ocean into the air, trailing long curtains of falling water.
13-17s, ABOVE THE STORM: The turtle climbs through the black clouds, with lightning flashing around it, and breaks through into total calm: a silver sea of moonlit clouds under a giant moon, stars and a soft green aurora. The rain stops at once. Glowing voxel jellyfish and small manta rays drift in the air around it, and the village lights glow on its back.
17-20s, THE RETURN: The boat's lantern rocks gently in the harbor. The turtle banks in a slow, graceful arc and glides down into the clouds. The white cloud fill hides the reset, and the cycle restarts seamlessly at the storm.

SCALE IS THE KEY: The boat must look tiny and the turtle truly colossal. Sell the size with slow, heavy movement, tiny details on the shell, and waterfalls that seem to fall in slow motion. The boat and its lantern stay visible as the reference point throughout.

WATER AND SKY: Build the ocean from an instanced voxel heightfield with layered animated waves, whitecaps, foam and a deep teal-to-black gradient. Use instancing for rain, spray, clouds and falling water. Lightning should light the scene from a realistic direction and cast brief shadows.

TURTLE: A detailed voxel model with a hexagonal plated shell, wrinkled skin and independently jointed head, neck and flippers. Parts of the shell glow softly with bioluminescent patterns once it is above the clouds.

MOOD AND LIGHT: Cold, violent blue-black during the storm; warm orange lantern, window and lighthouse light as the emotional anchor; peaceful silver, green and violet above the clouds. Add bloom, soft shadows, voxel ambient occlusion, volumetric light in the lighthouse beam, and subtle camera shake in the storm that fades to perfect stillness above the clouds.

CAMERA: One continuous shot with no cuts. Start low and close to the boat, pull far back during the reveal, rise with the turtle through the clouds, then settle into a wide side view of its full silhouette against the moon. Keep the action centered, with extra headroom at the top of the frame.

Everything must be procedural, with no external assets, and run smoothly in a browser. Make it as detailed and polished as possible.

title: Alpine Sunrise Oil Painting Process
author: hasif_dev
prompt:
Paint a majestic alpine mountain landscape at sunrise as a realistic oil painting, entirely from scratch in code, and show it being painted stroke by stroke.
A towering snow-covered mountain rises above a deep glacial valley, its jagged peaks catching the first golden light of dawn. Wisps of mist drift between dark pine forests, a turquoise river winds through the valley, and a rustic wooden cabin glows warmly beside the water. The upper peaks burn with amber sunlight while the lower slopes remain submerged in cool blue shadows. Tiny waterfalls tumble down sheer cliffs, wildflowers cling to the foreground rocks, and a few distant birds glide through the luminous morning sky.
Make it look like a masterpiece by a great landscape painter: extraordinary atmospheric perspective, physically convincing natural light, rich oil pigments, expressive brushwork, layered glazes, textured canvas grain, and thick impasto on sunlit snow, sparkling water, and illuminated foliage. Every rock, cloud, tree, reflection, and mountain ridge should feel deliberately painted, with beautiful color relationships and convincing depth.
Show the entire painting process from a completely blank, primed canvas:
Lay down the warm canvas ground and loose charcoal composition sketch.
Establish the dark underpainting and broad tonal masses.
Block in the mountain silhouettes, valley, forests, river, and sky with large visible brushstrokes.

Build up successive layers of color, atmospheric haze, snow textures, and reflected light.
Refine the trees, rocky surfaces, flowing water, distant peaks, and delicate foreground details.
Finish with confident, thick impasto highlights, luminous glazes, and small, precise final strokes.
Animation requirements: This must be a genuine procedural painting animation, not a finished image fading in or appearing all at once. Render actual brushstrokes progressively onto the canvas, with each stroke remaining visible as the painting develops. Use evolving stroke sizes, pressure-like variations, natural pigment mixing, bristle textures, and layered paint accumulation. The canvas should begin completely blank, and the finished masterpiece must be fully painted at exactly 25 seconds.
Technical constraints: Use only code and native drawing primitives. No external images, image textures, libraries, frameworks, imported assets, or pre-rendered artwork. Generate every brushstroke, texture, reflection, cloud, and lighting effect algorithmically. Keep the animation smooth, the composition coherent, and the rendering efficient.
Quality goal: Aim for the visual richness of a museum-quality traditional oil painting, with cinematic sunrise lighting, intricate natural detail, convincing depth, and an artistically sophisticated composition. Avoid generic procedural patterns, repetitive textures, flat vector shapes, and synthetic-looking gradients. Every stroke should contribute to the illusion of a real painter working on a physical canvas.
Make the final scene breathtaking enough to stand on its own as a finished work of art, while ensuring the painting process itself is just as beautiful to watch.

title: Continuous Camera Documentary Explainer
author: Cryptoxorz
prompt:
我想要一个完全用代码构建的电影式动态视频。没有AI视频生成器，也没有库存素材。每一帧都应该用代码绘制（HTML canvas 可以），并渲染成 MP4。

输入（附件）：
脚本/画外音：[附上音频文件] —— 行时序：[粘贴每行及其起始时间，或让 Claude 从音频中推算出来]
真实人物/地点/物体的照片：[已附上]
风格参考：[已附上 —— 这些展示了我想有的外观，匹配它们的氛围]
格式：[例如 21:9、3840x1646、30fps] —— 时长必须与画外音完全匹配。

风格：
整个视频是一个连续的相机移动，跨越一个大世界：一张地图、一张桌子、一块板子，无论什么适合故事。没有剪切，也没有幻灯片切换。相机平滑滑行、推进细节、拉回旅行，然后再次潜入。
运动必须感觉平滑且像拍摄一样。每个开始和停止都要缓入缓出。相机绝不突然停止：在保持时，它会继续缓慢漂移向即将去的方向。添加细微的手持运动、快速移动时的运动模糊、胶片颗粒、柔和辉光和晕影。
真实照片和文档作为物理物体（打印件、纸张、剪报）掉落到世界中，放置在故事发生的位置。

叙事和可读性规则（最重要的）：
每行叙述一个想法。每行在屏幕上获得一个主角（一张照片、一个词或一个文档），其他一切都淡化到后面。
每个短语在屏幕上只出现一次，绝不重复。如果叙述者说了它，要么在真实文档上展示它，要么在屏幕上打字显示，绝不两者兼有。
没有填充文本。文档上的正文应该是柔和的灰色线条，看起来像纸张，而不是人们试图阅读的文字。
大而易读的字体：主角词非常大，标签绝不细小。如果有人在一秒钟内无法在手机上读到它，它就太小了或内容太多了。
少即是多。省略不属于故事的装饰杂物（随机的胶带、邮戳、备忘录、多余标签）。
视觉时刻精确落在口述词上：当词被说出时画一个圆圈，在节拍上猛击一个邮戳。

流程：
在构建之前，写一个节拍表：时间 → 叙述 → 屏幕上的一个主角 → 任何屏幕文本。给我看，并询问任何不清楚的地方。
慢慢来。质量比速度更重要。优先考虑设计、平滑运动和清晰度，而不是添加更多东西。
在最终渲染之前，检查自己的工作：查看每个节拍的静态图像和相机移动的帧序列。修复任何杂乱、难读、重叠、或突然抖动/停止的东西。
交付最终的 MP4，带有同步的我的画外音，按照上述确切格式。

title: Voxel Mascot Build and Burst Loop
author: 0xFizzu
prompt:
Build a voxel mascot loop. One HTML file, three.js 0.160.0 via jsDelivr importmap, Geist Mono from Google Fonts. 1920x1080, 12 s at 60 fps (720 frames), frame 720 equals frame 0.
window.renderAt(t) draws any frame from t alone; seeded random only; ?t= freezes it.

Set: a white round plinth (radius 14) on an F4F2EE backdrop, 96 progress segments around its top edge, E4E0DA off, FF6A2B on.
Hero: the pixel Claude mascot as 1,200 rounded voxels in one InstancedMesh: D97757 body 14x10x8, two 2x2x4 arms, four 2x3x2 legs, 0F0F0F 2x4 eyes on the front face; ±5% tint per voxel, roughness 0.45, clearcoat 0.3.
Build, 0.1 to 3.1 s: voxels rain in layer by layer, bottom up, each falling 26 units in 18 frames (accelerating), scaling in from 0 and landing with a small bounce. The ring fills with the count. The eyes click in last, on frames 196 and 200.
Alive, 3.5 to 7.2 s: blink on 214; crouch 1.12x0.78 on 236; a hop 9 high with a 360° spin from 252 to 282; squash on landing, spring at damping 0.55. Wave the right arm from 300 to 360, pivoting at the shoulder: 70° up, ±25°, three swings.
Look left then right from 366 to 404, eyes sliding 0.75; blink again on 410. A 1.2% breath throughout.

Burst, 7.2 s: every voxel flies out 9 to 22 units along its direction from the centre, ease-out over 54 frames, tumbling; the cloud swirls about y, slowly speeding up.
Lift, 9.3 to 11.7 s: voxels spiral up and out of the top of the frame, pulling in 55% and accelerating, staggered by height; the ring drains as they go. Frame 720 is the empty plinth again.
Label, top left, Geist Mono 32 px: “0000 / 1200 VOXELS”, the live count; under it VOXEL MASCOT / 16:9 / 12 S LOOP in 8E8A83. Top right: a stage chip (READY, BUILD, BLINK, HOP, WAVE, LOOK, BURST, SWIRL, LIFT), FF6A2B while active, and a frame counter.
Camera: FOV 24, 16° elevation, ±12° orbit over 12 s, 10% push-in from build end to burst, tilt up 3 units for the cloud. Light: warm key front left, cool rim back right, ACES. Post: 9% vignette, 2% grain. Checks: render frames around every beat and the loop seam.

title: Marshmallow Forest Camp Night Film
author: aimarvis
prompt:
Build a single self-contained HTML file: a 30-second, 1920x1080 film of a tiny forest camp at night, made entirely in code.

Rules
- No images, no 3D model files, no texture files, no fonts, no external assets of any kind. Every tree, rock, the water, the fire, the sky and the character are generated in code. The only import allowed is three.js 0.170 from jsDelivr (importmap, three + three/addons).
- WebGL2 only (no WebGPU). It must render correctly in headless Chrome.
- Deterministic: expose window.ready (a Promise that resolves once everything is built and every shader is compiled) and renderAt(t) (draws the exact frame at t seconds, 0 <= t <= 30). Seeded randomness only, never the clock. Frames are captured one by one at 30 fps.
- The bar: a frame someone would mistake for a still from a high-end animated film or a photo, not a "cool WebGL demo".

The world
- A small clearing on the shore of a still mountain lake, deep in a pine forest, on a clear night. Low moon, a band of stars, faint mist on the water.
- A camp: a low A-frame canvas tent, a log bench, a ring of stones with a campfire (unlit at first), a stack of firewood.
- The lake is a mirror: it reflects the treeline and the stars, and later the fire.

The character
- Mochi: one toasted marshmallow, the size of a coffee mug in this world, sitting on the log. Soft, slightly translucent white body (light glows through the edges), golden-brown toasted top that fades into the white, a few fine caramel cracks. Face: two glossy black oval eyes with a white highlight, a small open smile, soft pink blush on the cheeks. Cute, but rendered as a real object, like a premium food commercial shot for an animated short.
- Mochi holds a phone. At the start its screen is the only bright, cold light in the scene.

The story (30 s)
- 0-6 s: Night. Blue phone light on Mochi's face, everything else nearly black. Slow push in. Mochi blinks.
- 6-9 s: Mochi lowers the phone and lays it face down on the log. The screen light dies. Near-darkness: only the stars and their reflection.
- 9-14 s: A spark. The campfire catches. Warm light floods the clearing, the tent glows, the reflection turns gold.
- 14-24 s: The forest wakes: fireflies rise from the grass and drift over the water, smoke curls up. The camera slowly orbits from behind Mochi toward the lake.
- 24-30 s: Wide shot from across the lake: the camp small and warm inside the dark forest, Mochi by the fire, the whole scene doubled in the water. Calm enough to work as a poster frame.

Look
- Physically based lighting, ACES tone mapping, soft shadows from the fire, fog, warm fire orange against cold moonlight blue.
- Post: bloom on the fire, fireflies and phone; subtle depth of field; light film grain; vignette. Cinematic, never neon.
- Camera moves like a real dolly: slow and steady. No text on screen.

title: Halloween Pumpkin Keyboard Animation
author: leohuanfang
prompt:
Make a 17-second vertical (1080x1920, 30 fps) Halloween animation with sound, using only code. No video model, no image model, no audio samples.
Draw every pixel on an HTML canvas, synthesize every sound in Python (numpy), render frame by frame with a headless browser, mux with ffmpeg at -14 LUFS.
Core rule: every sound must be caused by something you can see.
- A ghost hops from pumpkin to pumpkin. Each landing lights that pumpkin's face and plays its note. 9 pumpkins = 9 pitches like a keyboard: 7 orange in front (A3 B3 C4 D4 E4 G4 A4), 2 white behind (Bb3, D#4). Note names under each pumpkin.
- From ~3 s: three tombstones jump on every beat = bass.
- From ~6 s: the moon pulses = kick; bats beat their wings = hi-hat.
- Chorus: lightning = clap; 8 more ghosts burst out of the graves and land on the chord's pumpkins = organ chord stabs.
Music: Grieg, "In the Hall of the Mountain King" (1875, public domain), A minor. Play the 4-bar theme twice as one accelerando (eighth note 0.22 s -> 0.12 s), then a snare roll + riser,
then 0.75 s of near silence (screen goes dark, the ghost hangs mid-air, caption "WAIT…"). Chorus at ~2/3 of the video: flash, crash, full organ chord, pumpkins catch fire. End on one big A-minor hit with all 9 ghosts landing at once.
Loop it: after the final hit the other ghosts fly off and the first ghost jumps back onto pumpkin A, landing exactly on frame 0.
Captions (top third): first frame "A GHOST PLAYS / THE PUMPKINS / Claude Opus 5.5 wrote every frame and every note" with sound at 0.0 s; then "THE GRAVES ARE THE BASS", "BATS = HI-HAT / MOON = KICK", "WAIT…", "EVERYBODY OUT!", "HAPPY HALLOWEEN / name the song?".
Compute all events in Python first, save them to JSON, and make the canvas a pure function renderAt(t) of that JSON, so picture and sound can never drift apart.

title: Fold Paper 42 Times Explainer
author: 0xvosss
prompt:
GROK + JEV + OPUS 5.5 checked how thick a sheet of paper gets if you fold it 42 times, and it ends up past the Moon...

a normal sheet is 0.1 mm. fold it in half, then again. 42 times

most people guess a few metres

question → explain → check → calculate → animate

Grok took the explanation: every fold doubles the stack. so each fold adds more than all the folds before it put together

Jev checked the math: 0.1 mm × 2⁴² = 439,805 km. the Moon is 384,400 km away

Opus 5.5 ran every fold

10 folds: 10 cm, a phone
17 folds: 13 m, a 4-storey house
23 folds: 839 m, taller than Burj Khalifa
27 folds: 13 km, above Everest
30 folds: 107 km, edge of space
42 folds: 439,805 km, past the Moon
51 folds: 225 million km, past the Sun

the strange part: after 39 folds you're only 14% of the way. the last 3 folds do 88% of the trip

where this actually shows up:

you can't really do it. the record is 12 folds, set by a student in 2002 with a strip of paper over a kilometre long

the chessboard story: 1 grain of rice on the first square, double on each next one. the board ends with about 18 quintillion grains

anything that doubles looks like nothing for a long time, then like everything at once

0.1 mm, 42 folds, 439,805 km ↓

save this

title: Physically Based Ocean Flyover
author: hubery_bu
prompt:
Opus5.5仍然是最好的模型
过去一个月我使用Opus5.5在 three.js 上搭了一套基于物理的实时渲染管线：FFT海洋、物理大气、全局光照、体积云、体积雾……
我认为这完全达到了3A游戏以及电影级的游戏画面
在过去这需要一整个3A游戏工作室的美术团队才能做出来的效果，而今天一个普通人+AI就能做出这样的画面效果
仓库已开源，下面分享一下我是怎么做的

先说个事实
大部分3A游戏走的是「风格化写实」
风格化写实的核心在于
底子是物理的
材质、光照都按真实世界的数值来
风格放在选什么内容、几个跟着天气和时段走的光照参数、后期调色几个地方

工欲善其事，必先利其器
想要做出3A级的游戏画面
首先需要建立一套渲染管线
我照着公开的论文、技术分享，还有虚幻引擎公开的做法
在 three.js 上搭了一整套基于物理的实时渲染管线
FFT海洋、物理大气、全局光照、体积云、
GTAO、体积雾、自动曝光、局部色调映射…

但这只是把上限打开了，理论上能做到3A游戏的画面
有了物理底子之后
你还需要调曝光、色调映射、环境光强弱、雾的浓度、调色等等一大堆参数

所以我们还需要参考图
想要3A的画面，就必须拿真正3A游戏的画面当参考图
想要电影感，就拿电影
而且最好自己进游戏截图，时段、天气、构图都拍好
这一步AI可能帮不了你

有了参考图之后，是最后一步，也是最关键的一步
对照参考图「拟合」
把画面交给数学，而不是感觉（不管是AI的感觉，还是人的感觉）
我们需要对照参考图，用最小二乘来拟合
最小二乘做的事：
1. 找一组参数，让“参考图的测量值”和“我们渲染图的测量值”之间的差，平方加起来最小。
2. 这些差就是数据点。比如一张参考图上，被太阳照亮的草地、阴影里的草地、太阳附近的天空、远处的海面，每块区域量出亮度、彩度、色相，就是几个数。
3. 十几张参考图乘以每张七八块区域，就有上百个点。
4. 改参数、重新渲染、再量，优化器根据差怎么变，去找最好的那组参数。

→ every raindrop, spark and puff of smoke is a function of time

what broke: the first render turned the canal into gibberish. window frames bent by the waves looked like random glyphs. the fix was drawing each reflection row twice, 2px apart, at lower opacity. his waving hand was also stuck behind his own pumpkin

most "loops for hours" demos never show the seam. i diffed the last frame against the first: the jump is the same size as between any two neighboring frames

add 3 lines to the original prompt:
"render at 480x270, scale 4x, no smoothing"
"every animation must divide a 120s loop, particles are pure functions of time"
"add one character with a tiny story that plays out across the loop"

title: Earliest Program Was Cloth
author: thinkszyg
prompt:
最早的程序，是写给一块布的。

两千年前，汉代有人把字织进了丝绸。不是绣，不是印，是一根线一根线织出来的。

凑近看，它是二进制：经线在上记 1，纬线在上记 0。
· 平纹就是 1010。
· 斜纹每一行错开一格（你的牛仔裤就是）。
· 缎纹把交点打散，浮线拉长，所以发亮。
· 罗把两根经线绞在一起——这是 0 和 1 写不出来的那一种。
· 锦最难：每一格露五种颜色里的哪一种，都要提前定好。

古人把这些「定好的」编进一束打了结的线里，叫花本。《天工开物》（1637）写：织工根本不知道会织出什么花，「梭過之後，居然花現」。

1804 年，雅卡尔把花本换成打孔卡；巴贝奇把打孔卡用进了分析机；1843 年，Ada Lovelace 写下「分析机编织代数的图案，就像雅卡尔织机编织花与叶」。打孔卡，后来变成了程序。

这条片子怎么做的：
全片由 Claude Opus 5.5 完成——调研、脚本、约 1150 行画面与声音代码、混音、渲染、自动验收。我只负责定选题、选画风、提意见。
· 画面：795 行 JavaScript 在 Canvas 上逐帧绘制，每根丝线都按「经在上为 1」画出，片尾那段代码就是本片源码。
· 声音：222 行 Python，古筝、古琴、琵琶用物理建模合成，织机和打孔卡的声音程序生成，112 BPM 卡拍。
· 没有 AI 生图、没有 AI 生视频、没有素材库视频；文物照片来自大都会艺术博物馆公有领域藏品。
· 耗时：第一版约 45 分钟，按意见改 3 轮约 40 分钟；5432 帧在一台 Mac 上 77 秒渲完。

出处：大都会艺术博物馆 65598 / 50231 / 54408 / 222531（1839 年雅卡尔丝织像，用 24000 张打孔卡织成）；《天工开物》（1637）；Lovelace Note A（1843）；新华网 2018（中国丝绸博物馆复原五星锦，10470 根经线）。

翻开袖口看看：平纹、斜纹，还是缎纹？
